column32: According to the Tasmanian Government website (as last updated on 10 January 2022), eligible Tasmanians who lost income for reasons related to COVID-19 were able to access a range of income support measures provided by the Federal Government and the Tasmanian Government.    The Federal Government offered the Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment, a lump sum payment for some eligible individuals who lost income whilst isolating due to contracting COVID-19 or being a close contact of a COVID-19 case.    The Tasmanian Government offered several different assistance grants:    A $250 lump sum payment was offered to Tasmanians who lost income whilst isolating to wait for a PCR test result. This could only be claimed a maximum of once within a 30-day period. The 27 January 2022 version of the Tasmanian Government webpage stated that this PCR test payment could no longer be claimed at the same time as the Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment, but it is unclear exactly when this new rule was implemented.  Similarly, those who lost income as a result of receiving a COVID-19 vaccine, experiencing COVID-19 vaccine side effects within 3 days after being vaccinated, or caring for a dependant who had received the COVID-19 vaccine, could also receive a $250 payment.    Tasmanians who were unable to access the Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment, and lost income whilst  isolating due to contracting COVID-19, being a close contact of a COVID-19 case, or caring for a dependent who was a COVID-19 case or close contact, could receive the Pandemic Isolation Assistance Grant. This was a payment of $750 for every 7-day period of isolation, and Tasmanians could receive a total of $1500 if they were required to isolate for 14 days.    Those who lost income as a result of being required to quarantine after entering Tasmania could receive a $750 lump sum payment for each period of up to 7 days that they were in quarantine. This payment could only be claimed a maximum of once within a 30 day period.    Typically, Tasmanians could only be eligible for the aforementioned income support payments if they were unable to access paid sick leave or carers leave entitlements, and were not receiving any other form of Australian Government income support.    The income support measures available between 22 and 29 January 2022 were a continuation of existing relief measures, except for the changes to the PCR test payment, which represented a weakening of income support policy. column34: According to the Tasmanian Government website (as last updated on October 2021, but current as of 28 and 29 January 2022), there were no specific debt or contract relief measures offered by the Tasmanian Government for households affected by COVID-19. Although emergency accommodation was available for homeless families, or those who could not quarantine safely, this was not a form of rent or contract relief. column43: According to the Tasmanian Government website (as of 24 January 2021), all Tasmanians who were experiencing COVID-19 symptoms, were close contacts of a COVID-19 case, or were directed to get a COVID-19 test by Public Health were urged to take a COVID-19 test.    Tasmanians could either take RATs or PCR tests, and one Tasmanian Government webpage stated that COVID-19 PCR testing clinics should be used by individuals who were not able to take a RAT , or were specifically directed to get a PCR test by Public Health. However, in another Tasmanian Government webpage, several drive-through PCR testing clinics did not specify testing requirements or eligibility criteria, stating that individuals could simply turn up to get tested.    Therefore, although it is unclear whether Tasmanians who were symptomatic or close contacts could take a PCR test without fulfilling any other criteria in practice, the PCR testing directions in place between 22 to 29 January 2022 were a continuation of existing policies. column45: According to the Tasmanian Government website between 24 and 29 January 2022, individuals with COVID-19 were told to 'help with contact tracing', and were responsible for informing close contacts,  social contacts, as well as their places of employment and education that they were infected.   Businesses and workplaces were not listed as exposure sites, and were instead responsible for informing workplace contacts about positive cases, as well as implementing the necessary COVID-safe measures to keep employees safe. They were expected to assist with the contact tracing process by collecting staff or visitor information not provided by the Check In Tas app. However, Public Health would only contact a business if they knew of several cases linked to the business in question.    On 28 January 2022, the Tasmanian Government website was updated to remove a statement which explained that a 'close contact' could include an individual who spent more than 4 hours at the same site, workplace, or venue as a COVID-19 case during a significant transmission event. The new version of the website only stated that a 'close contact' was someone who spent more than 4 hours in a residential setting with a COVID-19 case during their infectious period.    The contact tracing in place between 22 and 29 January 2022 was a continuation of existing measures, although the change in the definition of a close contact represented a relaxation of existing measures, and an indirect reduction of government involvement with potential contacts of COVID-19 cases. column52: According to the Tasmanian Government website (as last updated on  20 January 2022), masks were mandatory for all Tasmanians above the age of 12 in all indoor public spaces and at large outdoor events attended by over 1000 people.     Masks were not required outdoors (except for at large events), at home (or when visiting the home of someone else), when working alone in an indoor space, when performing or rehearsing for a performance, in situations where clear enunciation or visibility of the mouth was required for employment, receiving a service that cannot be received whilst wearing a mask, travelling in personal vehicles, doing intense exercise, whilst being married, and in emergency situations where wearing a mask would pose a safety risk.    The directions in place between 22 and 29 January were a continuation of existing restrictions. column55: According to the Tasmanian Government website as of 29 January 2022, the Pfizer (Comirnaty) and Moderna (Spikevax) COVID-19 vaccines would be available to all Tasmanians 12 years old and above, whilst the AstraZeneca (Vaxzevria) COVID-19 was available to those 60 years and above.  Children between 5 and 11 years of age were able to receive a smaller dose of the Pfizer vaccine which was a third of the adult dose, at dedicated clinics across the state.    As 94.90% of Tasmanians over 12 had received two doses of a COVID-19 vaccine and 45.12% of children between 5-11 years old had received their first dose of a COVID-19 vaccine as of 29 January 2022, it is highly likely that the Tasmanian Government was able to provide vaccines for eligible age groups.     Pfizer and Moderna booster vaccines were available to Tasmanians 18 years old and above, provided that at least four months had passed since the second dose of their primary course of COVID-19 vaccine. Immunocompromised individuals could receive a third dose of a COVID-19 vaccine between two and six months after their second dose, as part of their primary course of vaccination.    All COVID-19 vaccines were provided free of charge. column12: According to an update published by the Tasmanian Government  on 25 January 2022, additional industries which were considered 'essential for the supply of critical goods and services to the community', such as health, welfare, care, and support industries, as well as education and childcare services, telecommunications, data, broadcasting, and media services, were able to register for a temporary exemption framework for close contacts from 28 January 2022. Critical staff working in these industries who were close contacts of a COVID-19 case were not required to quarantine if their business was undergoing a critical workforce shortage and had successfully registered for the framework.    Before registering for the framework, businesses were required to conduct a risk assessment to identify the risks of a critical workforce shortage, seek possible alternatives to requesting close contacts to fill the shortage, understand the minimum number of workers needed to provide their services, ensure that the return of the close contact is necessary and justified, implement extra measures to prevent the transmission of COVID-19 whilst the close contact is required to work, and establish a process to ensure the employer is aware once the critical shortage has passed and close contacts can resume quarantine or isolation.    Critical workers could only be granted an exemption if they were fully vaccinated, did not have COVID-19 symptoms, had their attendance registered through Worksafe Tasmania, and returned a negative COVID-19 test result each day before work.    This update was a relaxation of existing COVID-19 policy directions. All other workplace restrictions pertaining to COVID-19 remained the same:    The Tasmanian Government website (as last updated on 4 January 2022, and current as of 28 January 2022) stated that business were allowed to operate, but were required to implement measures to meet minimum COVID-19 safety standards and record them in a safety plan. According to the Direction Under Section 16 - Workplace COVID Plan - No.2, these minimum standards included the following:    	- Maintaining a physical distance of 1.5m where possible, or a density limit of 1 person per 2 square limits (unless the workplace was exempt from doing so)  	- Reviewing public health advice regularly in order to find ways to keep the business COVID-safe, as well as training workers to minimise the risk of COVID-19 transmission in the workplace, and informing patrons of COVID-related safety measures and restrictions  	- Cleaning and disinfecting the workplace as necessary to reduce the risk of COVID-19 transmission  	- Preventing individuals with COVID-19 symptoms, or those who are required to quarantine or self-isolate, from entering the business  	- Collecting contact information from individuals entering the workplace for contact tracing purposes (unless exempt from doing so)    Businesses were encouraged to review and update their Workplace COVID Plans as of 20 January 2022.    Masks were required in all indoor spaces and outdoor events attended by more than 1000 patrons, except where an individual had to perform a job that required clear enunciation or mouth visibility.    Unvaccinated patrons (i.e. those who had not received both doses of a COVID-19 vaccine at least 2 weeks ago) were prohibited from entering pubs, bars, nightclubs, outdoor events attended by over 500 people where visitors would be drinking while not seated, and indoor events attended by over 250 people where visitors would be drinking whilst not seated. Stadiums, arenas, theatres, cinemas, sporting clubs and community clubs were exempt from this requirement. Unvaccinated individuals were also prohibited from entering residential aged care facilities unless they had tested negative for COVID-19 (see H8 for more details). Evidence of vaccination status could be provided through a COVID-19 digital certificate,   Immunisation History Statement from the Australian Immunisation Register, or a similar document recognised by the Australian Government or Director of Public Health.      Note: Workers were required to be vaccinated at some businesses including quarantine facilities, health care settings, aged care and disability settings, and at licensed settings (such as pubs, clubs, bars, and nightclubs). Individuals working in early childhood education setting were required to have received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine from 8 January 2022. This information was not recorded in C2 or V4 as of 5 February 2022. As of 30 January 2022, the following travel directions apply:  Fully vaccinated travellers, or those with an exemption, do not need to register to enter Tasmania or undertake COVID-19 testing prior to arrival. However, any traveller who has spent time in an extreme-risk area in the 14 days before they plan to enter Tasmania, must seek approval.  There are no areas declared extreme risk between 28 January and 5 February 2022, but if you have spent time in an extreme-risk area and have been approved to enter, you must:  •	return a negative result on a COVID-19 rapid antigen test within 24 hours before departure or a PCR test within 72 hours before departure  •	only arrive at an approved entry point  •	quarantine for 7 days in a suitable premises or government-managed facility  •	travel directly to quarantine wearing a face mask and using private transport  •	have a COVID-19 rapid antigen test or PCR test on days 1 and 5 after arrival  As of 19 January 2022, all vaccinated travellers will no longer be required to register their travel or to take a COVID-19 test prior to travelling.    Unvaccinated travellers must apply for approval to enter Tasmania. If you arrive in Tasmania without approval, you will be directed to enter quarantine at a government-managed facility while your application is assessed. If it is not approved, you will be directed to leave the State. Fines may also apply  Approved unvaccinated travellers must meet arrival conditions including:  •	arrive at approved entry points  •	quarantine in suitable premises or a government-managed facility if suitable premises are not available  •	minimum five days quarantine but up to 14 days (dependent on results of required testing)  •	a COVID-19 rapid antigen test or PCR test on day five of your arrival in Tasmania  The arrival and testing requirements for Flinders and King Island are the same as for entering Tasmania with no additional requirements to arrive on the islands. However a traveller who is required to quarantine in a government-managed quarantine facility (e.g. an unvaccinated or unapproved arrival without a suitable premises) must not arrive at King Island, Flinders Island or any island in the Furneaux group of islands without the approval of the Deputy State Controller. This is because there are no government-managed quarantine facilities on the islands. column32: There are no regional variations of the following policies.  As of 30 January 2022, individuals are able to apply through Service Australia for Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment. Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment is a lump sum payment to help you during the time you can’t work and earn income because you have to self-isolate or quarantine for one of the following reasons:  •	you have coronavirus (COVID-19)  •	you’re a close contact of a person who has COVID-19  •	a child you care for who is 16 years or under, is a close contact of a person who has COVID-19  •	you’re caring for someone who has COVID-19  •	you’re caring for someone with disability or a severe medical condition who must self-isolate or quarantine because they’re a close contact of a person with COVID-19.  For each 7 day period of self-isolation, quarantine or caring, Service Australia will pay:  •	$450 if you lost at least 8 hours or a full day’s work, and less than 20 hours of work  •	$750 if you lost 20 hours or more of work.  •	If you lost less than 8 hours or a full day’s work during the 7 day period of self-isolation, quarantine or caring, you won’t be eligible for this payment.    Specifically within TAS, the following individual grants are available for people who lose income due to COVID-19.  -	You may be eligible for a $250 PCR test payment from the Tasmanian Government to help cover lost income or earnings while isolating and waiting for a PCR test result.  -	You may be eligible for a $250 Vaccination Payment from the Tasmanian Government if you lose income or earnings to get a COVID-19 vaccination, or because you experienced side effects from a COVID-19 vaccination within three days of being vaccinated. You may also be eligible if you lost earnings or income due to a dependant receiving a COVID-19 vaccine.  -	If you cannot access the Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment, you may be eligible for a $750 Tasmanian Government Pandemic Isolation Assistance Grant. You must be: a confirmed case or close contact of someone with COVID-19; or required to care for a dependant who is a confirmed case or close contact.  -	You may be eligible for support under the Tasmanian Government’s Pandemic Isolation Assistance Grant if you need to quarantine after returning to Tasmania. A grant of $750 for each period of up to seven days of quarantine is available to Tasmanian residents who have been directed under the Emergency Management Act 2006 (Directions in Relation to Persons Arriving in Tasmania), to quarantine for five to 14 days after returning to the State. column27: There are no regional variations of the following policies.  As of 6 February 2022, the following travel directions apply:  Fully vaccinated travellers, or those with an exemption, do not need to register to enter Tasmania or undertake COVID-19 testing prior to arrival. However, any traveller who’s spent time in an extreme-risk area in the 14 days before they plan to enter Tasmania, must seek approval.  If you have been in an extreme-risk area and have been approved to enter, you must:  •	return a negative result on a COVID-19 rapid antigen test within 24 hours before departure or a PCR test within 72 hours before departure  •	only arrive at an approved entry point  •	quarantine for 7 days in a suitable premises or government-managed facility  •	travel directly to quarantine wearing a face mask and using private transport  •	have a COVID-19 rapid antigen test or PCR test on days 1 and 5 after arrival    Unvaccinated travellers must apply for approval to enter Tasmania. If you arrive in Tasmania without approval, you will be directed to enter quarantine at a government-managed facility while your application is assessed. If it is not approved, you will be directed to leave the State. Fines may also apply  Approved unvaccinated travellers must meet arrival conditions including:  •	arrive at approved entry points  •	quarantine in suitable premises or a government-managed facility if suitable premises are not available  •	minimum five days quarantine but up to 14 days (dependent on results of required testing)  •	a COVID-19 rapid antigen test or PCR test on day five of your arrival in Tasmania  The arrival and testing requirements for Flinders and King Island are the same as for entering Tasmania with no additional requirements to arrive on the islands. However a traveller who is required to quarantine in a government-managed quarantine facility (e.g. an unvaccinated or unapproved arrival without a suitable premises) must not arrive at King Island, Flinders Island or any island in the Furneaux group of islands without the approval of the Deputy State Controller. column58: As of 25February 2022, the Tasmanian Government has implemented a number of measures to protect elderly people.  -All persons visiting a residential aged care facility, must wear a face mask while they remain on the premises. column55: According to the Australian Government Department of Health website (as last updated 3 February 2022), the Australian Government had been distributing COVID-19 vaccines through Operation COVID Shield, the national taskforce coordinating the Australian vaccine rollout.    As part of the rollout, all Australians* aged 5 years and over could book a free COVID-19 vaccination appointment, although it was slightly more difficult for those in the 5-11 year age group to receive a vaccine compared to other eligible age groups, as not all vaccine providers were able to provide the smaller Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine dose for 5-11 year olds.    The Pfizer (Comirnaty) COVID-19 vaccine was available for individuals aged 5 years and above, the AstraZeneca (Vaxzevria) COVID-19 vaccine was available to individuals aged 60 years and above (or 18-59 year olds who had chosen to take the vaccine after consulting with a healthcare professional), and the Moderna (Spikevax) COVID-19 vaccine was available to individuals 12 years and above. The Novavax (Nuvaxovid) COVID-19 vaccine was also available to those aged 18 years old and above after being provisionally approved by the TGA on 20 January 2022.    Booster vaccines were available for individuals aged 16 years and above who had completed their primary course of COVID-19 vaccination at least 3 months ago. 16-17 year olds could take the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine as part of their booster dose, and those aged 18 years and above could either take the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine or the Pfizer COVID-19 for their booster shot.    Immunocompromised individuals could also take a third primary dose of a COVID-19 vaccine.    As 93.65% of Australians aged 16 years and above had received two doses of a COVID-19 vaccine, 77.11% of Australians aged 12-15 years old had received two doses of a COVID-19 vaccine, and 44.15% of Australians aged 5-11 years old had received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine, the Australian Government was likely able to deliver on its universal vaccination policy. Nonetheless, State and Territory Governments also delivered their own updates and specialised services to meet the needs of their jurisdictions.    The directions in place between 30 January and 5 February 2022 were a continuation of existing directions.      *For the purposes of the vaccine rollout, Australian = those living in Australia    Archived links:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220214115310/https://www.health.gov.au/initiatives-and-programs/covid-19-vaccines/about-rollout  https://web.archive.org/web/20220126100654/https://www.health.gov.au/initiatives-and-programs/covid-19-vaccines/getting-your-vaccination/locations  https://web.archive.org/web/20220129073055/https://www.health.gov.au/initiatives-and-programs/covid-19-vaccines/who-can-get-vaccinated  https://web.archive.org/web/20220201192548/https://www.health.gov.au/initiatives-and-programs/covid-19-vaccines/who-can-get-vaccinated/children  https://web.archive.org/web/20220201022840/https://www.health.gov.au/initiatives-and-programs/covid-19-vaccines/getting-your-vaccination/booster-doses  https://web.archive.org/web/20220131131114/https://www.health.gov.au/initiatives-and-programs/covid-19-vaccines/approved-vaccines/novavax  https://web.archive.org/web/20220214120409/https://www.health.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2022/02/covid-19-vaccine-rollout-update-5-february-2022.pdf

column27: Vaccination, screening, and permits are not required for interstate travellers. column29: International travellers are required to have either an international COVID-19 vaccination certificate or a valid foreign equivalent. Travellers who are vaccinated or aged 12 years and under are required to quarantine at home or other private accomodations until they have received a negative test result. In the first 7 days of arrival (reduced from the 14 days previously required), they are required to carry proof of ID, their international passenger arrival permit, their test result, and evidence that they are fully vaccinated or exempt, and present these on request to authorities if asked.  https://web.archive.org/web/20220218182356/https://www.coronavirus.vic.gov.au/information-overseas-travellers
column32: The Victorian government offers a variety of one-off payments and support packages for individuals and businesses negatively impacted by COVID-19. column34: One-off rent relief grants are available for tenants who are facing rental hardship due to COVID-19. column52: Wearing a mask is required for everyone aged 8 and above in all indoor settings in Victoria with exceptions for being in a home, consuming food or drink, or receiving beauty services. column55: Vaccination is available for everyone aged 5 years and over. Those aged 12 years and over can have the Pfizer or Moderna vaccine. column58: Residents at care facilities, including aged care, can have up to five visitors per day if the visitors show evidence of a negative result from a rapid antigen test taken on the day of the visit. column32: As of 29 March 2022, the Australian Government continued to offer Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment (PLDP) for eligible workers. People who are unable to work and lost at least 8 hours or a full day’s work in a 7 day period of self-isolation, quarantine, or caring are eligible for this PLDP.   For each 7 day period of self-isolation, quarantine, or caring, people would receive $450 if they've lost at least 8 hours or a full day’s work, and less than 20 hours of work; or $750 if they've lost 20 hours or more of work.  According to Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS; 2022), the median weekly earnings in Australia were $1,209.00 for all employees, and the median hourly earnings were at $36 per hour. column12: WA has a mandatory COVID-19 vaccination policy for a majority of occupations and workforces in WA. The policy follows the existing mandates in place for workers in high-risk industries. Health care workers had to be fully vaccinated by December 2021, while other industries had to be fully vaccinated prior to this point as well (e.g., hotel quarantine workers, port workers).    Since January 4, proof of vaccination has been required for a number of higher risk venues and events in Perth and Peel, as part of a safe transition from the Delta backpacker cluster.    Proof of vaccination is currently required in Perth and Peel to enter the following venues:    - Nightclubs  - Music events (above 500 people) and specified high risk events  - Pubs, taverns, hotels (hospitality): With a capacity of greater than 500 patrons; or With a licence that allows them to operate after midnight  - A place operating under a special facility license: With a capacity of greater than 500 patrons; or With a licence that allows them to operate after midnight  - A place operating under an occasional liquor licence (licensed for 250 or more patrons)  - The gaming floor of the Perth Crown Casino.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220118142320/https://www.wa.gov.au/government/covid-19-coronavirus/covid-19-coronavirus-what-you-can-and-cant-do  https://web.archive.org/web/20220211003311/https://www.wa.gov.au/government/covid-19-coronavirus/covid-19-coronavirus-mandatory-covid-19-vaccination-information  https://web.archive.org/web/20220211013447/https://www.wa.gov.au/government/announcements/wa-proceed-safe-transition-plan-february-5-2022

column29: From 12.01am, Monday 15 November, 2021, travellers from low risk jurisdictions will need to be fully vaccinated. column32: According to the Services Australia website (as last updated on 20 January 2022), eligible Australians who suffered financial hardship because they were required to quarantine or self-isolate as a result of having COVID-19, being a close contact of someone with COVID-19, or caring for someone who was required to quarantine or self-isolate were able to receive the Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment or the Crisis Payment for National Health Emergency (COVID-19).     The Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment could be received by individuals who were not receiving any income support payments, were not able to access paid leave entitlements, and had less than $10,000 (AUD) in liquid assets.   Those claiming the payment for periods of mandatory isolation after 18 January 2022 could receive $450 if they had lost between 8 hours (or a full day's work) and 20 hours of work, or $750 if they had lost more than 20 hours of work.   Those claiming the payment for periods of mandatory isolation between 9 December 2021 and 17 January 2022 could receive $750 for each 7-day period of quarantine or isolation.  Those claiming the payment for periods of mandatory isolation before 8 December 2021 could receive $1500 for each 14-day period of quarantine or isolation.     The Crisis Payment for National Health Emergency (COVID-19) could be granted to individuals who were receiving or eligible for an income support payment or the ABSTUDY Living Allowance, and were experiencing severe financial hardship. It was equal to a week's pay at the maximum basic rate of the recipient's income support payment or allowance. Individuals could claim a maximum of 2 payments during a 6-month period, or a maximum of one payment per isolation period.     A 50% reduction in the minimum superannuation drawdown rate which was implemented by the Federal Government in May 2021 continued to be in place.     The directions in place between on the 22 Janurary to 30 Janurary were a continuation of existing directions. column32: According to the Services Australia website (as last updated on 20 January 2022), eligible Australians who suffered financial hardship because they were required to quarantine or self-isolate as a result of having COVID-19, being a close contact of someone with COVID-19, or caring for someone who was required to quarantine or self-isolate were able to receive the Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment or the Crisis Payment for National Health Emergency (COVID-19).    The Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment could be received by individuals who were not receiving any income support payments, were not able to access paid leave entitlements, and had less than $10,000 (AUD) in liquid assets.   Those claiming the payment for periods of mandatory isolation after 18 January 2022 could receive $450 if they had lost between 8 hours (or a full day's work) and 20 hours of work, or $750 if they had lost more than 20 hours of work.   Those claiming the payment for periods of mandatory isolation between 9 December 2021 and 17 January 2022 could receive $750 for each 7-day period of quarantine or isolation.  Those claiming the payment for periods of mandatory isolation before 8 December 2021 could receive $1500 for each 14-day period of quarantine or isolation.    The Crisis Payment for National Health Emergency (COVID-19) could be granted to individuals who were receiving or eligible for an income support payment or the ABSTUDY Living Allowance, and were experiencing severe financial hardship. It was equal to a week's pay at the maximum basic rate of the recipient's income support payment or allowance. Individuals could claim a maximum of 2 payments during a 6-month period, or a maximum of one payment per isolation period.    A 50% reduction in the minimum superannuation drawdown rate which was implemented by the Federal Government in May 2021 continued to be in place.    The directions in place between 30 January and 5 February 2022 were a continuation of existing directions. column32: As of 29 March 2022, the Australian Government continued to offer Pandemic Leave Disaster Payment (PLDP) for eligible workers. People who are unable to work and lost at least 8 hours or a full day’s work in a 7 day period of self-isolation, quarantine, or caring are eligible for this PLDP. column60: Change in validity of Janssen vaccination certificates 03 January 2022  From January 3rd, 2022 vaccination certificates for a one-time Janssen vaccination will be shown as invalid when checked within Austria. In order for affected persons to receive a valid vaccination certificate, a further vaccination is required no earlier than 28 days after the first vaccination. For further vaccination, an EMA-approved mRNA vaccine (BioNTech / Pfizer or Moderna) should preferably be used.    Information can be found under Recommendations for further corona vaccinations: 3rd vaccination or 2nd vaccination after COVID-19 vaccine Janssen ("Johnson & Johnson")    •  Recovery + 1st dose of Janssen from Johnson & Johnson  For people who have recovered before the vaccination, however, there is still the option of submitting a combination of a recovery certificate (separation notice, medical certificate or recovery certificate) and the 1/1 Janssen vaccination certificate as valid 2G proof.    •  Entry with 1/1 vaccination certificate with Janssen from Johnson & Johnson  Entry into Austria is still possible with a 1/1 Janssen certificate, as there is no change in the entry regulations. For entry from a virus variant area according to Appendix 1 without quarantine, a “booster” is required in addition to the PCR test (max. 48 hours old).    Please note that once you have entered Austria, you do not have a valid vaccination certificate during your stay in Austria!    The one-time vaccination Janssen allows entry, but not a visit to a restaurant, because within Austria the one-time vaccination is no longer recognized as 2-G proof.    Source: https://archive.fo/JYJX7#selection-1371.0-1477.165 [Coronavirus - Current Measures]

column9: School operations from January 10, 2022 - the safety phase will be continued.  In order to be able to maintain presence operation as a constant, the security phase will be extended until Saturday, February 26, 2022.    The most important measures at a glance  •	The schedule remains the same.  •	Parents and legal guardians are given the opportunity to leave their children at home without a certificate. An apology from the parents is sufficient, no medical certificate is required.  •	Pupils who are absent from school due to their parents' wishes can find out more about the subject areas from the responsible teachers (for example as part of a face-to-face lesson). There is no comprehensive distance learning, since the lessons are always face-to-face.  •	If the technical requirements are met, the students can take part in the lessons virtually on their own initiative. There is no obligation to do so.     Written performance assessments such as schoolwork or tests can take place in accordance with the hygiene measures according to the teachers' assessment. column60: 6th amendment to the 6th COVID-19 Protective Measures Ordinance is introduced (valid until January 20, 2022).    Regulations from January 11, 2022  FFP2 masks have so far proven to be an effective means of protecting against infection with the coronavirus. Against the background of the increased transferability of the Omikron variant, special emphasis is placed on the effectiveness of FFP2 masks. Therefore, from January 11, 2022:    •	FFP2 mask requirement also outdoors  Wherever the recommended minimum distance of two meters from people outside the household cannot or is not observed, an FFP2 mask requirement now also applies outdoors. This does not apply to situations where the minimum distance of two meters is only briefly exceeded, such as when simply "walking past" the sidewalk or during sports, etc.    •	Obligatory 2G control in non-essential retail establishments  The operators must check the customers' 2G evidence when entering the respective establishment - but at the latest when purchasing the goods.    •	Home office  Due to the increased risk of infection from the Omikron variant, there should also be a significant reduction in contacts at the workplace and employees should generally work from home wherever possible.    •	Pregnant people without 2-G evidence  Pregnant people who do not have valid 2-G evidence may instead show a negative PCR test (valid for 72 hours from sampling). column43: Testing is widely available, however, there have been bottlenecks in getting PCR results returned.  Updated legislation (7th amendment to the 6th COVID-19 Protection Measures Ordinance) which includes details on testing is introduced on 21 January.     Regulations from January 21, 2022  The lockdown for people without valid 2-G proof will be extended by a further 10 days (ie until January 31, 2022) due to the ongoing high and currently very sharp increase in basic epidemiological events. If it can be proven that the result of the molecular biological test (e.g. PCR) does not arrive in time due to the fault of a third party, in situations in which a 2G+ proof is required, the result of an antigen test for personal use that is no more than 24 hours old can now also be submitted. However, the tests must be recorded in an official data system. column60: 21 January - new amendment to the 6 . COVID-19 Protection Measures Ordinance is introduced: 7th amendment with validity until January 30th, 2022    Changes at https://archive.vn/j3Tmv. If it can be proven that the result of the molecular biological test (e.g. PCR) does not arrive in time due to the fault of a third party, in situations in which a 2G+ proof is required, the result of an antigen test for personal use that is no more than 24 hours old can now also be submitted. However, the tests must be recorded in an official data system.    In addition, the regulations that have been in force since January 11, 2022 remain valid:    FFP2 masks are also mandatory outdoors  Wherever the recommended minimum distance of two meters from people outside the household cannot be maintained or is not maintained, FFP2 masks are now also mandatory outdoors. Exceptions to this are situations where the minimum distance of two meters is only briefly exceeded, such as when simply "walking past" the sidewalk or during sports, etc.    Mandatory 2G control in business premises of non-essential trade  The operators must check the 2G proof of the customers when entering the respective business premises - at the latest, however, when purchasing the goods.    Home office  Due to the increased risk of infection through the Omikron variant, there should also be a significant reduction in contacts at the place of work and employees should generally work from home wherever possible.    Pregnant persons without a 2-G proof  Pregnant persons who do not have a valid 2-G proof may instead present a negative PCR test (valid 72 hours after sampling). column12: At work  •	The professional activity should preferably take place outside the workplace, if this is possible and both employer and employee agree.  •	Employees, owners and operators may only enter workplaces where physical contact with other people cannot be ruled out with a 3G ID. (A maximum of two physical contacts per day, outdoors and lasting no longer than 15 minutes each, are not considered contacts).  •	An FFP2 mask should be worn if physical contact with people cannot be ruled out or the risk of infection can be minimized by other suitable protective measures.  •	Owners of a place of work with more than 51 employees must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.  •	With regard to the wearing of a mask and the submission of proof of a low epidemiological risk, stricter regulations that go beyond this Ordinance can be provided for in justified cases.  •	If it can be credibly demonstrated that a negative PCR test cannot be presented for reasons of lack of availability, an untimely evaluation or due to the unpredictability of the official activity to be performed, operators may exceptionally admit persons even if they have 3G proof submit. This also applies to operators.    **Customer areas**  •	 Commercial premises and (body-related) services may only be entered with a valid 2G ID. Operators must check the 2G proof of customers in customer areas - for the purpose of purchasing goods or using services - if possible upon entry, at the latest when purchasing goods or using the service.  •	Exceptions to the 2G obligation are establishments providing basic services, such as: public pharmacies, grocery stores and farmers' direct sellers, drugstores and drugstores, banks, petrol stations  •	The FFP2 mask requirement applies in closed rooms in the customer area of business premises as well as the connecting structures of structurally connected business premises (e.g. shopping centers, market halls).  •	Operators must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.  •	Business premises may only be open between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.    **Gastronomy and accommodation**  Gastronomy  •	The gastronomy is open to customers with a valid 2G card.  •	Customers must be assigned a seat. The business premises may only be entered between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.  •	Food and beverages may not be consumed in the immediate vicinity of the dispensing point and only while seated at the administration points. Outdoors, food and catering stands at administration points may also be consumed while standing.  •	The FFP2 mask requirement applies in closed rooms, but not while staying at the administration site.  •	Operators must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.  •	Self-service is permitted provided that the risk of infection can be minimized through special hygienic precautions.  •	The collection of food and non-alcoholic beverages as well as alcoholic beverages in commercially sealed containers is permitted for everyone with an FFP2 mask, regardless of 2G proof. The food and drinks may not be consumed within a radius of 50 meters from the business premises.    Accommodation  •	Accommodation establishments (including campsites and shelters) may only be entered with a 2G ID.  •	When entering, the FFP2 mask requirement applies.  •	An exception to the 2G proof obligation can be made for the absolutely necessary period if a 3G proof is provided and if:  	o	Persons who were already being accommodated at the time this provision came into force, for the duration of the accommodation agreed in advance with the accommodation provider,  	o	for the purpose of caring for and providing assistance to people in need of support, professional reasons that cannot be postponed, satisfaction of an urgent need for housing, spa guests or patients in a spa or rehabilitation facility.  •	Exceptions apply to pupils for the purpose of attending school and students for study purposes.  •	Operators must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.    **Leisure, sports and culture**  Leisure  Access to leisure facilities (such as leisure and amusement parks, swimming pools, dance schools, facilities for practicing prostitution, animal parks, etc.) is only permitted for people with a 2G card.  •	The FFP2 mask requirement applies in closed rooms  •	Opening hours are only allowed between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.  •	Operators of leisure facilities must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.    Arts and Culture  Access to art and cultural institutions (museums, art galleries, cultural exhibition halls, libraries, libraries, archives, theatres, cinemas, variety shows, cabarets, concert halls and arenas) is only permitted with a 2G ID.  •	The FFP2 mask requirement applies in closed rooms  •	Opening hours are only allowed between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.  •	Operators of leisure facilities must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.    Sports  •	Entering sports facilities for the purpose of practicing sports is only permitted under certain conditions:  	o	There is a 2G proof for non-public sports facilities and an FFP2 mask requirement in closed rooms.  	o	 The opening hours of sports facilities are only permitted between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.  	o	Without 2G proof, sports may only be practiced outdoors in public sports facilities. column55: In order to successfully combat the corona pandemic and protect the Austrian health system, a high vaccination rate is necessary. (A maximum of two physical contacts per day, outdoors and lasting no longer than 15 minutes each, are not considered contacts).  •	When entering the workplace, an FFP2 mask must be worn unless physical contact with people is excluded or the risk of infection cannot be minimized by other suitable protective measures.  •	Owners of a place of work with more than 51 employees must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.  •	With regard to the wearing of a mask and the submission of proof of a low epidemiological risk, stricter regulations that go beyond this Ordinance can be provided for in justified cases.  •	If it can be credibly demonstrated that a negative PCR test cannot be presented for reasons of lack of availability, an untimely evaluation or due to the unpredictability of the official activity to be performed, operators may exceptionally admit people if they instead have one from a present a negative antigen test (valid for 24 hours) carried out by an authorized body.    **Customer areas**  •	In customer areas of business premises and the connecting structures of structurally connected business premises (e.g. shopping centers, market halls), customers in closed rooms are required to wear an FFP2 mask.  This also applies to entering  	o	Administrative authorities and administrative courts for party traffic, as well as  	o	for religious practice institutions.  •	Customers may only use body-hugging services with 3G proof.  •	Operators must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.  •	Entering customer areas is only permitted between 05:00 and 24:00 (with exceptions such as charging stations, pharmacies on call).    **Gastronomy and accommodation**  Gastronomy  •	The gastronomy is accessible to customers with a valid 3G card.  •	Customers must be assigned a seat.  •	The business premises may only be entered between 05:00 and 24:00.  •	Food and beverages may not be consumed in the immediate vicinity of the dispensing point and only while seated at the administration points. Outdoors, food and catering stands at administration points may also be consumed while standing.  •	The FFP2 mask requirement applies in closed rooms, but not while staying at the administration site.  •	Operators must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.  •	Self-service is permitted provided that the risk of infection can be minimized through special hygienic precautions.  •	The collection of food and non-alcoholic beverages as well as alcoholic beverages in commercially closed containers is permitted for everyone, whereby an FFP2 mask must be worn in closed rooms. The food and drinks may not be consumed within a radius of 50 meters from the business premises.    Accommodation  •	Accommodation establishments (including campsites and shelters) may only be entered with a 3G ID.  •	When entering, the FFP2 mask requirement applies.  •	An exception to the 3G proof obligation can be made for the absolutely necessary duration:  •	For persons who were already being accommodated at the time this provision came into force, for the duration of the accommodation agreed in advance with the accommodation provider,  •	for the purpose of caring for and providing assistance to people in need of support, professional reasons that cannot be postponed, satisfaction of an urgent need for housing, spa guests or patients in a spa or rehabilitation facility.  •	Exceptions to the 3G proof exist for entering an accommodation facility for pupils: inside for the purpose of attending school and for students for study purposes (boarding schools, dormitories for apprentices and student dormitories) for the absolutely necessary duration.  •	Operators must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.    **Leisure, art and culture, sport**  Leisure  Access to leisure facilities (such as leisure and amusement parks, swimming pools, dance schools, facilities for practicing prostitution, animal parks, etc.) is only permitted for people with a 2G card.  •	The FFP2 mask requirement applies in closed rooms  •	The opening times are only permitted between 05:00 and 24:00.  •	Operators of leisure facilities must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.    Arts and Culture  Regardless of 3G proof, anyone can visit cultural institutions such as museums, art galleries, cultural exhibition halls, libraries, bookshops and archives.  •	In general, the FFP2 mask requirement applies in closed rooms of art and cultural institutions.  •	Contact data is not collected.  •	Access to cultural institutions in which meetings mainly take place, such as theatres, cinemas, variety shows, cabarets, concert halls and arenas, is permitted with a 3G card.  •	Opening times are between 05:00 and 24:00.  •	Operators of leisure facilities and cultural facilities in which meetings mainly take place must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.    Sport  Entering sports facilities for the purpose of practicing sports is only permitted under certain conditions:  •	  	o	There is a 3G proof for non-public sports facilities and an FFP2 mask requirement in closed rooms.  	o	 The opening hours of sports facilities are only permitted between 05:00 and 24:00.  	o	The following applies to people without 3G proof when entering public sports facilities: Only outdoor sports facilities may be entered. Closed premises may only be entered with an FFP2 mask if this is necessary to practice the sport outdoors. Staying in the sports facility is limited to the duration of the exercise.  •	Operators of non-public sports facilities must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept.  •	elite sport:  	o	When sports are practiced by top athletes, a responsible doctor must draw up a COVID-19 prevention concept and compliance with it must be monitored on an ongoing basis.  	o	Top athletes, as well as their supervisors and trainers, must show proof of 3G for training and competitions if physical contact with other people cannot be ruled out.   	o	If a SARS-CoV-2 infection becomes known in an athlete, supervisor or trainer, all athletes, supervisors and trainers are to be in the following 14 days after the infection became known before each competition undergo a PCR test or an antigen test for the presence of SARS-CoV-2 infection. Gatherings  •	The following general measures apply to meetings:  •	The FFP2 mask requirement applies to meetings in closed rooms or outdoors.  •	Meetings may only take place between 05:00 and 24:00.  •	For gatherings without exclusively assigned and marked seating, entry is only permitted with a valid 3G credential.  •	Events with more than 50 people are only permitted if there is a ban on consumption (e.g. at family reunions, birthday parties, wedding celebrations, etc.). An FFP2 mask must be worn at all times.  •	Serving food and serving drinks is only permitted at meetings with up to 50 participants and with exclusively assigned seats.  •	Several meetings may take place at the same time in one place, provided that appropriate measures, such as spatial or structural separation or staggering in time, prevent the participants of the meetings taking place at the same time from mixing and the risk of infection is minimized.  •	The following also applies to meetings for rehearsals for professional purposes and for professional artistic performances in a fixed composition:  If it is not possible to wear a mask due to the activity, the risk of infection must be minimized by other suitable protective measures.  •	The FFP2 mask requirement applies to meetings held as part of the labor market service (retraining, etc.) and as part of other training and further education purposes (including final exams). If it is not possible to wear a mask due to the nature of the training or the integration measure of people, the risk of infection must be minimized by suitable protective measures.  •	For meetings of more than 50 people, organizers must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept. Excluded from this - as well as from the 3G proof obligation - are:  	o	funerals,  	o	assemblies according to the Assembly Act,  	o	Meetings for professional purposes if these are necessary to maintain professional activity,  	o	meetings of bodies of political persons that cannot be postponed, if holding them in digital form is not possible,  	o	meetings of bodies of legal entities that cannot be postponed, if holding them in digital form is not possible,  	o	meetings that cannot be postponed under the Labor Constitution Act,  	o	meetings of medical and psychosocial self-help groups,  	o	Driving into theatres, concert halls and arenas, cinemas, music halls and cabarets when this is done with multi-track motor vehicles.  •	The regulations for meetings do not apply to meetings for the practice of religion.  •	Personal assistance and 24-hour care are not included in the maximum number of persons or households.  •	There is an obligation to notify from 50 people and a permit from 250 people.  •	The measures mentioned also apply to trade and public fairs as well as occasional markets or demarcated areas of occasional markets. At occasional markets that offer goods, food or drinks for sale, 3G proof and an FFP2 mask requirement apply in closed rooms.  •	If it can be credibly demonstrated that a negative PCR test cannot be presented for reasons of lack of availability, an untimely evaluation or due to the unpredictability of the official activity to be performed, the operator or the person responsible for the meeting may also exceptionally if they instead present a negative antigen test (valid for 24 hours) carried out by an authorized body, or present a negative antigen test for self-testing that is recorded in an official data processing system (valid for 24 hours). Educational field  Tests or evidence of a low epidemiological risk  Schools are open to anyone who needs them. If students are in the school building and have no evidence of a low epidemiological risk (vaccinated, recovered or tested), they must carry out antigen or PCR tests at least twice a week. These tests must be carried out so often that for each day of the teaching week valid proof can be presented. If the test intervals are observed, the test result is also valid on the sixth and seventh day after the first test.    Mask requirement  •	In the generally accessible areas of the school building or in homes (e.g. corridors), teachers and administrative staff as well as external persons are still required to wear FFP2 masks.  •	From March 5th, 2022, the obligation to wear FFP2 masks in classrooms and group rooms and teachers’ and conference rooms for teachers and administrative staff as well as for external persons with proof of a low epidemiological risk (vaccinated, recovered or tested) will no longer apply.  •	Outside the classrooms and group rooms, students up to the 8th grade wear an MNS and students from the 9th grade wear an FFP2 mask.  •	A mask does not have to be worn in physical education classes, in movement-oriented classes in the classroom or in dormitories.    Extracurricular youth education, youth work and supervised holiday camps  •	Meeting rules apply  •	Employees in elementary educational institutions, facilities for extracurricular childcare and childminders are obliged to provide evidence of a negative PCR test twice a week (max. 72 hours from sample collection).    For further binding regulations see  COVID-19 School Ordinance 2021/22  and its  amendment   as well as  COVID-19 Higher Education Act .  Further information can be found on the website of the  Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF) . column60: COVID-19 Basic Measures Ordinance  From March 5th, 2022 (up to and including April 2nd, 2022), the COVID-19 Basic Measures Ordinance will be in force nationwide. Central areas are listed below, for further binding regulations see  COVID-19 Basic Measures Ordinance.      Gradual relaxation - Coronavirus: current measures  From March 5th, the following relaxations will come into force: In all essential settings in which the 3G rule previously applied, there will be no obligation to provide proof in future :  •	In hospitals, APHs and comparable settings, 3G applies to visitors, employees and service providers  •	FFP2 is still mandatory in the following areas:  	o	in hospitals, APHs and comparable settings  	o	in public transport including their stops  	o	in the customer areas of vital trade  	o	in administrative authorities for party traffic and connecting structures  	o	as well as the places of work in the above areas with direct customer or party contact  •	In all other places, there is still a recommendation to wear an FFP2 mask in closed rooms .  •	No general curfew  •	Opening of the night gastronomy  •	No person limits  •	Consumption permitted at events  •	The regulations for prevention concepts and COVID officers remain in place    The Basic Measures Ordinance will initially apply until April 2, 2022.    A number of restrictions are still in place in Vienna, although several have been lifted. column60: New regulations since March 24, 2022  In order to counteract the current burden on hospitals and to relieve hospital staff, the federal government has decided to make the following adjustments to the corona protection measures:  A general FFP2 mask requirement in all closed rooms:  •	in public places,  •	in means of transport,  •	throughout trade,  •	for physical services,  •	in gastronomy (on the way to the seat, not at the administration place),  •	in the accommodation,  •	in sports facilities (except when practicing sports),  •	in cultural and leisure facilities,  •	at places of work,  •	in retirement and nursing homes and  •	in hospitals.  For gatherings of 100 or more people without assigned seats ( ie  at parties, wedding celebrations  , etc. ), there is a  “choice of choice” between compliance with the mask requirement in closed rooms or a 3-G check . If organizers opt for the 3G rule, no FFP 2 masks have to be worn.  Exceptions to the general FFP 2 mask requirement:  •	in the private living area,  •	at the administration site (seated or standing),  •	at rehearsals or artistic performances in a fixed composition, professionally and privately ( ie theater ensembles as well as private brass bands and choirs) and  •	at meetings, also in gastronomy and night gastronomy, if it is a closed group.  night gastronomy:  •	Regulation as for meetings in closed rooms from 100 people, i.e. a "choice" for the operator between FFP 2 mask obligation or 3-G control  secretion:  From the 5th day of isolation, if you have been symptom-free for at least 48 hours, the isolation is over in the case of a mild course of the disease or asymptomatic infections. However, a traffic restriction applies for another 5 days. In order to have the traffic restriction lifted early, a free test can be carried out (negative  PCR test or CT value = 30). If the CT is <30, the traffic restriction must be continued until the end of the 5 days (or if a CT=30 is achieved before that).     Traffic Restriction:  •	Wearing an FFP 2 mask or a higher-quality mask when in contact with other people, even within private living areas,  •	No visits to facilities with vulnerable people or risky settings (e.g. retirement homes, health facilities)  •	No entry into facilities or no exercise of activities where an FFP 2 mask or an MNS is not worn continuously (catering establishments, fitness clubs , etc. ),  •	No attendance of major events and the like (sporting events, concerts, etc.)  •	Visiting the place of work  is generally possible, provided that the continuous wearing of an  FFP 2 mask and compliance with suitable protective measures can be guaranteed. column43: Test strategy  The low-threshold and comprehensive test offer will remain free of charge until the end of March . After that, corona tests will be used in a more targeted manner in Austria.     At the same time, access to free corona tests will continue to be made possible:   	•	From April 1,  people in Austria will be provided with a certain quota of free corona tests:  		o	5 free PCR tests per month  		o	5 free antigen tests per month  	•	In addition, there are still free corona tests  for  people with symptoms.  	•	People in vulnerable settings,  such as in hospitals or retirement and nursing homes, can be tested more often.  In order to continue to monitor the pandemic as broadly as possible, more focus will be placed on wastewater monitoring in the future. column45: Contact management  In view of the currently very high number of cases, many employers are currently facing the challenge that many people are falling ill at the same time or are in quarantine as contact persons. In order to counteract this burden, there is a change in the procedure for isolating contact persons. They are now subject to a traffic restriction for 10 days.    No contact persons are:  •	Persons if FFP 2 masks were worn on both sides during contact,  •	Persons with 3 immunological events ( e.g. 3 vaccinations),  •	Children up to 12 years of age with 2 immunological events, or  •	People who have recovered within the last 3 months (omicron recoveries).     Traffic Restriction:  •	Wearing an  FFP 2 mask  or a higher-quality mask when in contact with other people, even within private living areas,  •	No visits to facilities with vulnerable people or risky settings ( e.g. retirement homes, health facilities),  •	No entry into facilities  or no exercise of activities where  an FFP 2 mask  or an MNS is not worn  continuously  (catering establishments, fitness clubs , etc. ),  •	No attendance of major events and the like (sporting events, concerts, etc.)    Visiting the place of work is generally possible, provided that the continuous wearing of an  FFP 2 mask and compliance with suitable protective measures can be guaranteed.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20220328163936/https://www.sozialministerium.at/Informationen-zum-Coronavirus/Coronavirus---Aktuelle-Ma%C3%9Fnahmen.html

column58: Retirement and nursing homes as well as inpatient residential facilities for the disabled  In general, the FFP2 mask requirement applies to visitors, accompanying persons, employees, external service providers and residents (in places that do not belong to their own living area).    The following also applies to visitors:  •	Operators may only admit visitors and accompanying persons if they present proof of 3G (vaccinated, recovered or tested).  •	Excluded from this are persons accompanying underage residents of inpatient residential facilities for the disabled, as well as for visits by palliative and hospice patients, for pastoral care and to accompany critical life events.    The following also applies to residents:  •	3G proof (vaccinated, recovered or tested) must be presented for new admissions.  •	Residents can be offered an antigen test or PCR test by operators at least every seven days, and if they have left the home within this period, at least every three days.    The following also applies to employees:   •	Operators may only let employees in if they present proof of 3G (vaccinated, recovered or tested).  •	This also applies to external service providers, residents' representatives, patient, disabled and nursing advocates, nursing supervisory bodies or members of established commissions.    In principle, the planned measures must not be disproportionate or lead to unreasonable hardship.    **In Vienna**  The 2G+ rule applies to visitors.  •	2 visitors per day are possible per patient  •	FFP2 mask, hand hygiene  •	Palliative care and hospice support as well as pastoral care for critical life events are excluded from this.    **In Carinthia**  Inpatient residential and care facilities for the elderly  Since January 17, 2022 (until March 31, 2022), additional measures to prevent the spread of COVID-19 in inpatient residential and nursing homes have been in place:  •	Access is only permitted for visitors if they can show 2G+ proof that was not older than 48 hours.   •	For employees, the 2G proof or a negative PCR test that was taken no more than 48 hours ago applies; in exceptional cases, if this is absolutely necessary to maintain service operations, a negative PCR test that was taken up to 72 hours ago can also be accepted.  •	"Boosted" employees also have to show a negative PCR test once a week, employees without a booster vaccination three times a week.  •	The following applies to visitors and employees:  In the event of a positive PCR test result, entry into old people's and nursing homes is still permitted if there are at least 48 hours of symptoms after the infection has passed and based on the medical laboratory findings, in particular based on a CT value >30, it can be assumed that there is no longer any risk of infection.  •	The residents must be offered a PCR test at least once a week. column43: Change in testing strategy as of 1 April 2022.  The adjustment of the test strategy affects the previously free mass testing. In the future, 5 free PCR and 5 free antigen tests will be available to every citizen per month.    **New guidelines**  Test strategy  Austria is broadly positioned in terms of testing the population and has been able to establish a secure, functioning and nationwide test network. In order to be prepared for the coming challenges, the basic features of this test system should be retained. This means that new developments such as new virus variants can be reacted to    quickly if necessary .    At the same time, Austria is currently facing changed framework conditions due to the Omicron variant. Therefore, the Austrian test strategy - as a key pillar of pandemic management - is being adapted to the current situation: Against the background of higher immunity in the population, tests should now be used primarily where they are needed. Also, anyone who needs a test will get one! This means that tests for symptomatic people as well as tests for residents, visitors and employees of vulnerable areas will continue to be available free of charge and without restrictions.    Starting in April, the Austrian test strategy consists of three different test tracks. Funding will be provided by the federal government, but implementation and organization will remain the responsibility of the federal states, as has been the case up to now.    Symptomatic Individuals : Tests for symptomatic individuals will remain in place as usual. This means that the tests are still available free of charge and without restrictions for this group of people.     The first point of contact for symptomatic people remains 1450. The exact implementation is carried out by the individual federal states, which is why the process for those affected can vary from federal state to federal state.    Vulnerable Settings : The new test regulation defines vulnerable areas, for whose residents, visitors and employees as well as for companions and external service providers unlimited and free tests will continue to be available.  Here, too, implementation is carried out by the federal states.      Tests of the general public ("mass testing") : The adjustment of the test strategy affects the previously free mass testing. In the future, 5 free PCR and 5 free antigen tests will be available to every citizen per month :  5 PCR tests: starting April 1st.  5 antigen tests: Available from pharmacies from April 9th.  A temporary solution is provided for self-tests purchased before April 1st: Each person can have a total of 10 PCR tests evaluated by April 30th.  For all additional tests, the chargeable test offer in Austria can be used.    At the same time, wastewater monitoring will play a greater role in the future in order to be able to reliably and long-term monitor the course of the pandemic.    The adjusted test strategy will come into effect on April 1st and will initially be valid until June 30th.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20220403154843/https://www.sozialministerium.at/Informationen-zum-Coronavirus/Coronavirus---Aktuelle-Ma%C3%9Fnahmen.html

column9: How are the current, far-reaching easing of restrictions affecting university and college operations?  Not directly. Because the universities and colleges remain exempt from the general health law requirements and thus also from the current Corona Basic Measures Ordinance . However, they offer an important orientation for the individual and independent definition of those corona measures that the universities and colleges take independently and independently within the framework of their autonomy. These vary from university to university and from college to college.    This is also the reason why universities and colleges currently have different forms of access regulations (2.5G, 3G regulation or none at all) depending on their situation-specific requirements and why the handling of a mask requirement is quite different. In view of the general lifting of most restrictions, universities and colleges are also considering whether they should relax their corona measures even further, while also monitoring the epidemiological situation. In any case, the recommendation to wear an FFP2 mask in closed rooms remains.    Therefore, please find out from your respective university or college which corona measures must be observed at their locations.    Sources:   https://archive.ph/j9rGq [Coronavirus (COVID-19): Frequently asked questions and answers (FAQ) in the university and college sector]  https://archive.ph/FKBQD [5-point plan for getting back to normal at universities and colleges]
column12: At work  The FFP2 mask obligation applies when entering work places in closed rooms,  •	unless physical contact with people from outside the household is excluded, or  •	the risk of infection can be minimized by other suitable protective measures (in particular technical protective measures such as the installation of partitions or plexiglass walls).  •	The FFP2 mask requirement also applies to entering external workplaces, with the exception of those in your own private living area.  •	In justified cases, stricter regulations that go beyond the legal requirements can be made to prevent the further spread of COVID-19.    **Health and social sector**  Mobile care and support services  •	Mobile care and support service providers may only enter external workplaces if they can show proof of a low epidemiological risk (vaccinated, recovered or tested) and wear an FFP2 mask when in contact with customers.    Hospitals and health resorts and other places where health services are provided  The FFP2 mask requirement generally applies to patients, accompanying persons, visitors, operators, employees and service providers. unless the risk of infection can be minimized by other suitable protective measures.    The following also applies to employees:   •	Operators may only let employees in if they present proof of 3G (vaccinated, recovered or tested).  •	This also applies to external service providers, residents' representatives, patient, disabled and nursing advocates, nursing supervisory bodies or members of established commissions.  In principle, the planned measures must not be disproportionate or lead to unreasonable hardship.    Retirement and nursing homes as well as inpatient residential facilities for the disabled  In general, the FFP2 mask requirement applies to visitors, accompanying persons, employees, external service providers and residents (in places that do not belong to their own living area).  The following also applies to employees:   •	Operators may only let employees in if they present proof of 3G (vaccinated, recovered or tested).  •	This also applies to external service providers, residents' representatives, patient, disabled and nursing advocates, nursing supervisory bodies or members of established commissions.  In principle, the planned measures must not be disproportionate or lead to unreasonable hardship.    **COVID-19 officer and COVID-19 prevention concept**  Operators and owners of the following areas must appoint a COVID-19 officer and develop and implement a COVID-19 prevention concept:  •	cable cars and cog railways,  •	Coaches and excursion boats in occasional traffic,  •	Business premises with customer areas,  •	non-public sports facilities and leisure facilities,  •	workplaces with more than 51 employees,  •	Retirement and nursing homes as well as residential facilities for the disabled and  •	hospitals or sanatoriums    The COVID-19 prevention concept is a state-of-the-art concept for minimizing the risk of infection with SARS-CoV-2. A data protection-compliant system for the traceability of contacts, such as a system for recording the presence on a voluntary basis of visitors or accompanying persons and external service providers, can also be included for old people's and nursing homes as well as inpatient residential facilities for the disabled as well as for hospitals and spa facilities. column58: Health and social sector    Mobile care and support services  •	Mobile care and support service providers may only enter external workplaces if they can show proof of a low epidemiological risk (vaccinated, recovered or tested) and wear an FFP2 mask when in contact with customers.    Retirement and nursing homes as well as inpatient residential facilities for the disabled  In general, the FFP2 mask requirement applies to visitors, accompanying persons, employees, external service providers and residents (in places that do not belong to their own living area).    The following also applies to visitors:  •	Operators may only admit visitors and accompanying persons if they present proof of 3G (vaccinated, recovered or tested).  •	Excluded from this are persons accompanying underage residents of inpatient residential facilities for the disabled, as well as for visits by palliative and hospice patients, for pastoral care and to accompany critical life events. column29: Belgium operates a colour code that determines entry protocols based on the country of arrival. (Red(High risk), Yellow(Moderate risk) and Green(Low risk)). Stricter rules apply for countries considered to be Very High Risk.    People from countries categorized as "VERY HIGH RISK COUNTRIES" outside the European Union or Schengen area are not allowed entry into Belgium.     Vaccinated people from ZONES catorized at "RED" outside the European Union or Schengen area are required to get tested before your arrival in Belgium (PCR or RAT), regardless of the length of stay and to get also tested (PCR) on day 1 and 7 after arrival in Belgium. They would also have to stay in quarantine until the negative result of your test on day 1.    Those coming in from a GREEN or ORANGE zone do not need to get tested or quarantine. column52: Wearing a face mask remains mandatory for everyone in the following areas:    - on public transport from entering the indoor areas of the airport, the station, on the platform or a bus, (pre-)metro, tram, train stop or any other means of transport organised by a public authority. Public transport operators and all bus operators carrying out public transport services are not required to cover their nose and mouth, insofar as the driver is well-isolated in a cabin on the one hand, and a poster and/or sticker indicates to users the reason why the driver is not wearing a mask on the other;  - in the indoor areas of organised collective transport (i.e. transport organised in advance with a clear itinerary or final destination and a vehicle with at least 9+1 seats (passengers + driver)), this does not apply to public transport operators, insofar as the driver is well-isolated in a cabin on the one hand, and a poster and/or sticker indicates to users the reason why the driver is not wearing a mask on the other;  - in establishments and places where close-contact professions are carried out. This applies to service providers and customers where there is direct physical contact between the service provider and the customer or where the distance of 1.5 metres cannot be guaranteed between the service provider and the customer for a duration of at least 15 minutes;  - the publicly accessible areas of companies, associations and services;  the publicly accessible areas of commercial establishments, shops and shopping centres;  libraries, game and multimedia libraries;  - in the indoor areas accessible to the public of establishments belonging to the sports sector, including fitness centres and establishments that may remain open in accordance with Article 7, §1 of the Royal Decree, subject to items 11 and 12 below;  - in places of worship and buildings intended for the public practice of non-denominational moral services;  when moving around in public and non-public parts of courthouses and courtrooms and, in other cases, in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Chairman;  - the publicly accessible areas of government buildings;  establishments and places where catering activities are permitted, both for staff and those customers who are not seated at a table or at the bar;  locations where authorised private gatherings and activities in an organised context take place with more than 50 people indoors or 100 people outdoors;  - venues for events of any size, including mass events, authorised outdoor conferences and authorised sports competitions;  trade fairs, including exhibitions;  - other locations where access is organised in accordance with the Cooperation Agreement of 14 July 2021 with regard to the CST. *the indoor areas of schools and educational institutions;  - the indoor areas of the after-school care facilities for primary school children.    Archived: https://web.archive.org/web/20220127105912/https://www.info-coronavirus.be/en/faq/
