column34: On March 16 2022, the Harbin Municipal People's Government issues the "Implementation Measures for Several Financial Policies of Harbin City on Further Supporting Small, Medium and Micro-sized Enterprises and Individual Industrial and Commercial Households to Stable Production and Operation in Response to the Impact of the Epidemic", which mainly to clarify how the 2 billion funds for stabilizing and stabilizing jobs should be used. The policy mainly includes three aspects. First, implement the financial support policy for stabilizing enterprises and jobs, and encourage banks to grant loans to qualified small, medium and micro enterprises and individual industrial and commercial households through the implementation of a risk sharing mechanism for government bank guarantee institutions. The second part is to provide loan discounts to eligible enterprises. The third part is that the financing guarantee company funded by the municipal finance will reduce or exempt the guarantee fee for eligible enterprises. The scope of the financial support policy to stabilize stability and stability of jobs includes: small, medium, and micro enterprises (including individual industrial and commercial households) that have encountered difficulties in five industries, including wholesale and retail, accommodation and catering, cultural tourism, transportation and logistics, and manufacturing, which have been greatly affected by the epidemic. The loan discount policy supports: small, medium and micro enterprises and individual industrial and commercial households engaged in wholesale and retail, accommodation and catering, education, tourism, culture, sports and entertainment, transportation and other six industries in Harbin City. column12: From the Announcement No. 55 of Harbin's COVID-19 Work Headquarter, since March 19 2022, the following policy will be implemented.     1. In addition to farmers' markets, shopping malls, supermarkets, morning markets, pharmacies, gas stations, catering enterprises (only providing self-pickup, take-out ordering services) and other basic livelihood security business places, other business places and stores should all be closed.    2. Places that are allowed to operate must strictly implement various prevention and control measures, such as "scanning code, temperature measurement, wearing masks", staggered peak current limit, daily disinfection, employee health monitoring, and employees should hold a negative nucleic acid test certificate within 48 hours to go to work. Those who do not comply with the epidemic prevention and control regulations will be ordered to suspend business for rectification, and can resume operations only after passing the examination.    3. During the nucleic acid of all citizens in Harbin, all people entering the shopping malls, supermarkets, pharmacies, farmers markets, morning markets and other business places must hold a negative nucleic acid test certificate within 48 hours. Those who do not have a certificate are prohibited from entering. Localities can take necessary management measures according to the actual situation.     4. Express delivery and meals takeout companies should strengthen the health management of employees. All employees should undergo nucleic acid testing once a day. In principle, express delivery and meals takeaway companies' employees are not allowed to enter the residential area, and contactless delivery methods shall be implemented. Those who need to enter the communities should use smart express cabinets, post stations, etc. to deliver express deliveries must strictly implement measures such as "scanning code, temperature measurement, wearing masks", piece-by-piece disinfection, and strictly inspect delivery personnel for 24 hours Negative certificate of nucleic acid test.    5. During the nucleic acid testing of all citizens, all levels of government agencies, enterprises and institutions in Harbin shall strictly manage all entry and exit channels, strictly implement measures such as "scanning codes, measuring temperature, and wearing masks" for all entry personnel, and conduct inspections for 48 hours negative certificate of COVID-19 nucleic acid testing.    6. The business of various types of administrative examination and approval service halls, petition reception places and other window units in our city can be handled online or by self-service, all of which are handled in a "non-face-to-face" manner. And implement various epidemic prevention and control measures.    7. All kinds of enterprises should take the main responsibility for epidemic prevention and control, and strictly implement the "two points and one line" commuting mode.    See The Paper news website.    Archived: https://web.archive.org/web/20220323133745/https://m.thepaper.cn/baijiahao_17203544

column27: From the Announcement No. 57 of Harbin's COVID-19 Work Headquarter, since April 1 2022, the following policies will be implemented.    1. The Harbin city will liberalize travel restrictions on agricultural production in an orderly manner. The orderly and smooth the green channel of agricultural materials transportation will be implemented. Cross regional "point-to-point" transportation is allowed for vehicles transporting agricultural means of production and agricultural machines and tools. The drivers and passengers shall be managed in a closed manner throughout the whole process, and unloading and handover shall be conducted without contact. Among them, the transport vehicles from the districts in the Harbin city can be delivered to the designated place of the village for contactless delivery. Also, implement "landing detection" for drivers and passengers (if the "landing detection" has been carried out at the entry checkpoint, the detection will not be repeated). The vehicles shall be disinfected and escorted by special personnel to the designated place for contactless delivery. During the period, standardized personal protection shall be done. column9: On April 6, Pingyang County, Wenzhou City issued a notice,  1? The broad masses of citizens in the county do not leave Pingyang or go out of their homes unless necessary;  2? All schools in the county will be temporarily suspended, and all kinds of offline training will be suspended;  3? All public places in confined spaces in the county will be closed temporarily, and other public places, communities and vehicles will strictly implement measures such as temperature measurement, scanning "Wenzhou epidemic prevention code" and "place code", wearing masks and disinfection, and reasonably control the number of personnel;  4? Restaurants and restaurants in the county will cancel Hall Food and encourage customers to pack and take away consumption;  5? The county strictly implements the postponement of weddings, simple funeral and no banquet;  6? In addition to participating in the basic operation of the city, the staff of all organs and institutions in the county fully devote themselves to the front line of epidemic prevention and control on the basis of personal protection;  7? column9: On April 11, Haining, Zhejiang adjusted the emergency response of major public health emergencies to level II. All schools, kindergartens, childcare institutions and offline training institutions in Haining City have been temporarily suspended. Except for the necessary business places such as supermarkets and service stores, all other business places such as agricultural trade and life markets will be closed temporarily. All kinds of scenic spots are temporarily closed.  Suspend all kinds of literary and artistic performances, exhibitions, sales promotions and other activities. The "red business" is postponed, the "white business" is simplified, and the banquet is not allowed. Restaurants and restaurants are not allowed to eat in the hall, but only for takeout.  Strictly control all kinds of meetings, strictly control the number of participants and postpone the holding of meetings with more than 50 people in accordance with the principles of "no unnecessary holding", "online but not offline", "who is responsible for hosting", "where is responsible for hosting".  Strictly control the high-speed export, and suspend the entry of vehicles in addition to ensuring the transportation of key materials such as production, life and epidemic prevention; Hangzhou Hainan intercity railway, taxis, buses, long-distance passenger vehicles and other public transport were suspended.  http://archive.today/2022.04.13-134350/http://www.zj.chinanews.com.cn/jzkzj/2022 -04-11/detail-ihaxmqeq7515380. shtml  On April 11, a large number of hospitals in Ningbo were closed, and a large number of scenic spots were closed.  http://archive.today/2022.04.13-133230/https://www.163.com/dy/article/H4MRSJJ705259VI8.html

column12: Since 0:00 on April 12, the level II emergency response of public health emergencies in Tongxiang City has been adjusted to level III emergency response. Suspend the organization of large-scale square dance, aerobics and other gathering recreational activities.  Visits to nursing homes, welfare homes, psychiatric hospitals and other key places will be suspended. The results are presented at the various entry points in one of the official languages ??of Cameroon, namely French or English. All incoming travellers, aged 5 and over, are systematically tested at the Border Health Posts (PSF). Screening at the borders responds to the screening strategies defined by the country. column29: Testing/screening on arrival  All international travellers are subjected to extra, rapid flow, testing for Coronavirus on arrival at Yaoundé and Douala international airports. This is the Rapid Flow test. At present this includes all passengers arriving in Cameroon. These tests are compulsory. Results are returned while passengers are at the airport. There is no fee.    This is in addition to the requirement to have a negative PCR test 72 hours before embarkation on the first leg of your journey to Cameroon.    Quarantine requirements  If you have a proof of a recent (no older than 72 hours before boarding) negative coronavirus test, you will normally not have to self-isolate. Anyone that has developed symptoms of Coronavirus on their travel or tests positive on arrival at Yaoundé or Douala airport will be held for further enquiries to trace contacts and movements. We believe that anyone testing positive can quarantine at the location of your host or private accommodation until a negative PCR test is produced. These requirements are regularly evolving. column9: A number of COVID-19 measures continue in Cuba including social distancing, wearing a face mask in public and limited operations of businesses and public spaces. You should comply with restrictions at all times and follow the advice of local authorities. Mobility within and between provinces will also vary depending on the evolution of the pandemic, and may result in disruption to local and inter-province transport options, as well as curfews.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220307151941/https://www.dfa.ie/travel/travel-advice/a-z-list-of-countries/cuba/
column29: All visitors to Cuba will be required to complete a sworn health declaration (Declaración Jurada de Salud).    As of January 5, all visitors to Cuba must provide proof of a full course of vaccination eg: the EU DCC, as well as a negative PCR test, taken within 72 hours before travel. You should satisfy yourself that the test is administered by a certified laboratory in the country of origin.    Visitors under the age of 12 are exempt from providing vaccination certificates or PCR test results.    Public health initiatives such as spot PCR checks may be carried out at the airport, especially if you display symptoms of the virus. There are also limits on entry to the airport, with only passengers with proof of travel being allowed inside the airport terminal.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220307151941/https://www.dfa.ie/travel/travel-advice/a-z-list-of-countries/cuba/

column29: As of December 27, 2021 “TRNC” has classified the United States as a “Red” country. Vaccinated travelers from the United States entering by air or sea (see below for entering visa through UN Buffer Zone) who provide proof of vaccination (14 days after their final dose) or proof of recovering from COVID in the previous six months must also present a negative PCR test result in the previous 72 hours. Unvaccinated passengers must present a negative PCR test from the previous 72 hours and quarantine for seven days at their own expense. See the country categories here.  The PCR test result must be on paper (not SMS), be stamped by the lab or hospital conducting the test, include a barcode, and must be in English. Fully vaccinated travelers may cross with a negative rapid or PCR test in the previous seven days. Those allowed in home quarantine are monitored by electronic device. column9: Cyprus is changing its compulsory quarantine rules for school children in an effort to keep pupils in school amid surging coronavirus infections, the country's health minister said Wednesday. column29: Djibouti recently began enforcing a June 2021 Presidential Proclamation requiring all travelers 11 and older to Djibouti to present both a negative COVID PCR test carried out within 72 hours of commencing travel AND proof of a full course of COVID vaccine. Djibouti will NOT accept a letter of recovery from COVID-19. All travelers must present a negative COVID test to enter or board a flight to Djibouti.    Are health screening procedures in place at airports and other ports of entry? Yes.  All travelers must present a negative COVID test certificate within 72 hours of boarding any flight bound for Djibouti and not more than 120 hours prior to their arrival in Djibouti; all travelers will be screened upon arrival and must have a negative result in order to enter.  All travelers 11 and older must present evidence of a complete course of COVID vaccination.  Travelers coming to Djibouti by air/sea/land must be screened for COVID-19 upon arrival at ports of entry and the test must be negative in order for an individual to enter the country. Travelers testing negative but who do not present evidence of COVID vaccination will be subject to a mandatory home/hotel quarantine for an unspecified period. The Ministry of Health has suggested that all international travelers should quarantine for five days upon arrival in Djibouti.  Upon arrival at Ambouli International Airport, all passengers are tested for COVID-19 using a minimally invasive saliva test.  Travelers identified with the virus either go into isolation and treatment at a local hospital or quarantine at their hotel. Travelers will have to pay 5000 Fdj or $30 to cover the cost of the COVID-19 saliva test. Some travelers have reported that this process can take several hours to complete.  Travelers coming to Djibouti must be equipped with protective masks at the time of departure or arrival at the points of entry, respect the physical distance of one meter, if possible, at all stages of the journey and carry a hydro-alcoholic gel throughout the trip.  If a high percentage of passengers on a particular flight receive a positive saliva test, the Government of Djibouti may require all passengers to complete a second, nasal swab COVID-19 test.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220219181812/https://dj.usembassy.gov/covid-19-information/

column18: The Ministry of Tourism International Transport and Maritime Initiatives, through the Discover Dominica Authority (DDA), has decided to hold special entertainment events for Carnival 2022. Prime Minister of Dominica, Hon. Roosevelt Skerrit stated that Government, after numerous discussions and consultations with industry stakeholders, has approved protocols for special events. He explained that in the first instance, Government will look to pilot these number of special events which will occur between February 20 to March 1, 2022 and will only be made available to vaccinated citizens.  These events will be open only to fully vaccinated patrons and will be held at two approved venues, the Windsor Park Sports Stadium Forecourt and the Old Mill Cultural Center. The Windsor Park Sports Stadium Forecourt, will be designated as the main event venue, to accommodate a maximum of 500 patrons. The Old Mill Cultural Center will be approved for virtual events and cater for up to 200 patrons. No street jump-ups, village carnivals, unauthorized gatherings of groups and troops, or activities will be approved without having first applied for and received a permit. Approved activities are intended to be managed events for vaccinated patrons within a safe zone, to ensure the health and safety of patrons and the wider public. column9: Students returned to the classroom for the first time on Monday, March 7 since the start of the 2021/2022 academic year last September. The resumption of face to face classes was announced by Minister for Education, Human Resource Planning, Vocational Training and National Excellence, Hon. Octavia Alfred at a press conference on Friday March 4. According to her, Cabinet has decided that all primary and secondary schools will be open for in-person learning from Monday 7th March 2022, utilizing a blended approach, that is online and face to face. The general arrangement is that all form five and all Grade 6 students at all schools will be in daily, and the rest of the space at the schools will be used to rotate the rest of the school population. Small schools with a population of eighty students or less with adequate space for the stipulated 3 to 6 feet social distancing will be fully open. We have about four schools with less than 81 students but they do not have the required space so they will fall under the arrangement for schools with a population between 81 and 200 students. These schools will operate under a blended approach with grade six students coming in every day, while Grades K, 1, 2 and 3 come in from Mondays to Wednesdays, and Grades 4 and 5 on Thursdays and Fridays. All primary schools will operate from 9 to 2, however the primary schools who operate from 8 to 1 will continue to do so. At secondary schools all Form 5 students will be in Monday to Friday from 8 to 1. Forms 3 and 4 will go in Mondays to Wednesday forms 1 and 2 students will attend Thursdays and Fridays. The Dominica Grammar School and the Goodwill Secondary School will continue to work on shift. The Dominica Community High School has just 61 students and enough space to accommodate all the students every day. The days when children are not engaged online they will be doing face to face and the days when they are not at school they will be engaged online. column29: "Most travelers (for example, from United States, Canada, Argentina, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Panama, France, Germany, Italy, Russia, Puerto Rico, etc.) do not need to present a negative COVID-19 test upon arrival to enter the Dominican Republic. Airports and other ports of entry will perform a quick, aleatory breath test to a percentage of passengers, and all those who present symptoms, upon arrival. column32: 05/02/22    Algeria has been hit by two shocks in 2020—the spread of COVID-19 and the sharp decline in oil prices. Government policy is responding to both shocks.    The first case of COVID-19 in Algeria was reported on February 25, 2020. The authorities responded to the pandemic by implementing containment measures since early February 2020 (e.g., cancelling flights, and imposing quarantines to repatriated Algerians). Confinement measures included closure of schools, universities, restaurants, and shops; cancellation of public and private events; shut down of transportation services (internal and external); putting on mandatory leave half of civil servants and private workers with full compensation. Demonstrations and religious activities were cancelled, a lockdown of affected areas was ordered and a curfew was put in place in several cities including Algiers.    A gradual easing of containment measured started in early June 2020. The authorities have continued to monitor and adapt the lockdown measures as needed, including during the second wave of the pandemic in Algeria in late 2020. International borders partially reopened in June 2021. The number of daily new cases, which had fallen sharply through late March 2021 following a peak during the second wave, is ticking up again. Algeria started the vaccination campaign in late-January 2021 and has since received additional doses through the COVAX Facility and other sources for a total of 2.7 million doses as at end-May 2021. Domestic production of the Sputnik V vaccine is expected to start in September, according to an official government announcement.      Key Policy Responses as of June 28, 2021    FISCAL  In terms of tax measures, in response to the economic impact on households and enterprises of the lockdown measures in 2020, the authorities postponed the declaration and payments of income taxes for individuals and enterprises. Further contractual deadlines were relaxed and penalties for companies that experience delays in completing public contracts were suspended. Imports of pharmaceutical products and medical equipment used in the fight against Covid-19 were temporarily exonerated from VAT and custom duties.    The 2021 budget law introduced a permanent tax holiday for foreign-currency-generating export activities and suspended VAT and custom duties for imported or domestically purchased inputs used in the production of goods. It also extended the repayment period of overdue tax claims to 60 months from 36 months previously,    In terms of spending measures, a supplementary finance law (SFL) enacted on June 4, 2020 included provisions amounting to DZD 70 bn dinars to mitigate the health and economic impacts of the COVID-19 crisis. For the health sector, this included DZD 3.7 bn for medical supplies, DZD 16.5 bn for bonus payments to health workers, and DZD 8.9 bn for the health sector's development. For the economic impact, the law included DZD 20 bn for allowances to the unemployed and DZD 11.5 bn for transfers to poor households. Overall, in order to adjust to the new low oil price environment, the SFL envisaged a reduction in current and capital spending by 5.7 percent (representing 2.2 percent of 2019 GDP) compared to the initial 2020 budget law.    The government estimates the total budget cost of spending measures taken in response to the pandemic at DZD 238 bn for 2020 and the first four months of 2021. Of this amount, DZD 99.1bn were in exceptional bonuses to civil servants contributing to the fight against the pandemic, mostly health workers, DZD73bn were in social support measures to low-income households and DZD 22.5bn for vaccine procurement.    In terms of economic reforms, a national socio-economic recovery plan was discussed at a conference in August 2020. The authorities published a 2020-2024 Economic Revival plan in June 2021. Among other things the plan aims at diversifying the economy, fostering high value-added sectors and international trade and promoting a favorable business climate and FDI.    MONETARY AND MACRO-FINANCIAL   On March 15, the Bank of Algeria lowered the reserve requirement ratio from 10 percent to 8 percent, and its main policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.25 percent.    On April 6, the Bank of Algeria announced that it was easing solvency, liquidity and NPLs ratios for banks. Banks are also allowed to extend payments of some loans without a need to provision against them.    On April 30, the Bank of Algeria announced that it was cutting its main policy rate from 3.25 to 3.00 percent, that it was lowering its reserve requirement ratio from 8 percent to 6 percent, and that it was lowering haircuts on government securities used in refinancing operations.    On September 14, the Bank of Algeria announced a reduction in the reserve requirement ratio from 6 percent to 3 percent and the activation of 1-month open market operations.    On October 14, 2020, the Bank of Algeria announced that the easing of prudential requirements for banks, announced in April 2020, would be extended through the end of the year.    On January 6, 2021, the Bank of Algeria announced that the easing of prudential requirements for banks, first announced in April 2020, would be extended through March 31, 2021. On February 8 2021, the Bank of Algeria announced a reduction in the reserve requirement ratio from 3 percent to 2 percent effective February 15, 2021.    On April 1, 2021, the Bank of Algeria announced that the easing of prudential requirements for banks, first announced in April 2020, would be extended through June 30, 2021.    EXCHANGE RATE AND BALANCE OF PAYMENTS  The authorities announced several measures to cut the import bill by at least USD 10 bn (6 percent of GDP). Authorities banned exports of several products, including food, medical and hygiene items.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220205223224/https://www.imf.org/en/Topics/imf-and-covid19/Policy-Responses-to-COVID-19

column9: On Tuesday 30 November, the Ministry of Education announced the postponement of the return to school for those schools whose students had not returned to the classroom since the beginning of the pandemic due to the new variant of the coronavirus.    The postponement of dates implied that it will not be until 7 February 2022 that the centres of the Sierra-Amazonian system will return to 100% attendance, while those of the Coastal-Galapagos system will do so on 3 May, for the new 2022-2023 school year, which means that the latter will continue to be virtual until then.    About 48% of educational establishments nationwide are already working in face-to-face classes with reduced seating capacity, which represents around 675,193 students.    https://web.archive.org/web/20211202004342/https://www.elcomercio.com/tendencias/sociedad/unicef-lamenta-coe-reapertura-escuelas-omicron.html

column9: Schools are open, with regionally variable health measures in place including distancing and masking. Unvaccinated students who have close contact with an infected person must stay home from school and quarantine. Vaccinated students with a close contact may attend school as normal, but must test for Covid-19. If the test is positive they must take stepst to avoid transmission to vulnerable groups but are not obliged to quarantine or miss school.  https://archive.ph/kMnqq  https://archive.ph/vvIBI
column12: There is no general requirement to close workplaces. This typically includes bars, restaurants, and nightclubs but extends in some cases to other businesses like gyms, cinemas, concert venues, and hotels. column29: From 6 January, the classification of countries returns to the 3-stage system of Green/Orange/Red with the elimination of the temporary fourth "Scarlet Red" category. Countries of the travellers origin are categorised as follows:     "Green" countries/territories: countries/territories in which no active circulation of the virus is observed and no variants of concern are identified. These are the countries of the European area, to which are added Argentina, Australia, Bahrain, South Korea, The United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, Japan, Kuwait, New Zealand, Qatar, Rwanda, Saudi Arabia, Senegal, Taiwan, Uruguay and Vanuatu.    "Orange" countries/territories: countries/territories in which active circulation of the virus is observed in controlled proportions. These are all countries/territories not included in the lists of "green" and "red" countries/territories. Reinforced measures are in force for travel between France and the United Kingdom. The Travel Advice sheet for the United Kingdom should be consulted.    "Red" countries/territories: countries/territories in which active circulation of the virus with the presence of variants of concern is observed. These are: Afghanistan, Belarus, Botswana, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Georgia, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Moldova, Montenegro, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, South Africa, Suriname, Tanzania, Turkey, Ukraine, the United States, Zambia and Zimbabwe.    All passengers from Red list countries must present negative results of a PCR or antigen test taken in the previous 48 hours at boarding and may be tested again on arrival. Unvaccinated passengers are subject to presentation of "compelling reasons" for travel, mandatory antigen testing on arrival, and must quarantine for 10 days under the control of security forces.     Passengers from Orange list countries must present negative results of a PCR or antigen test taken in the previous 48 hours at boarding. Vaccinated passengers are not subject to the "compelling reasons" regime, but unvaccinated people are and must commit to self-isolation lasting 7 days and undergo testing at the end of this period.     Although an Orange list country, additional regulations apply to all passengers aged 12 or over arriving from the United Kingdom:     - subject to the list of "compelling reasons"  - must present a negative PCR or antigenic (TAG) test taken less than 24 hours before the flight on boarding ;  - must register before departure on the eOS-COVID digital platform  ;  - may be tested antigen on arrival ;  - will be subject to mandatory isolation for 10 days,supervised and controlled by the security forces. This isolation obligation may be lifted from 48 hours, subject to being able to justify a negative test (PCR or TAG).    Specific guidance for UK passengers is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220108054040/https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/conseils-par-pays-destination/royaume-uni/    Passengers from Green List countries are divided into two groups:     1. Member States of the European Union, Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Norway, San Marino, the Holy See and Switzerland - Travelers twelve years of age or older who do not have proof of a complete vaccination schedule or a certificate of recovery from Covid-19 must present before travel the negative result of a test (PCR or antigenic) of less than 24 hours. They may be tested for antigen on arrival.    2. Argentina, Australia, Bahrain, Hong Kong, Japan, Kuwait, New Zealand, Qatar, Rwanda, Saudi Arabia, Senegal, South Korea, Taiwan, The United Arab Emirates, Uruguay and Vanuatu:  All travelers twelve years of age or older, regardless of their vaccination status,from these countries/territories must present for boarding, the negative result of a PCR test or an antigen test (TAG) carried out less than 48 hours before the flight.     https://web.archive.org/web/20220108050616/https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/informations-pratiques/article/coronavirus-covid-19

column29: From 24 January, the classification of countries on the 3-stage system of Green/Orange/Red has been adjusted with some countires and territories moving from Red or Green status to Orange. Countries of the travellers origin are categorised as follows:     "Green" countries/territories: countries/territories in which no active circulation of the virus is observed and no variants of concern are identified. These are the countries of the European area, to which are added Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, South Korea, the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, Japan, Kuwait, New Zealand, Qatar, Rwanda, Senegal, Taiwan, Uruguay and Vanuatu. (previously, Argentina and Australia were on the Green list, but have moved to Orange)    "Orange" countries/territories: countries/territories in which active circulation of the virus is observed in controlled proportions. These are all countries/territories not included in the lists of "green" and "red" countries/territories. Reinforced measures are in force for travel between France and the United Kingdom. The Travel Advice sheet for the United Kingdom should be consulted.    "Red" countries/territories: countries/territories in which active circulation of the virus with the presence of variants of concern is observed. These are: Afghanistan, Belarus, the United States, Georgia, Mauritius, Montenegro, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Suriname, Tanzania, Turkey. (previously, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Moldova, Mozambique, Namibia, Russia, South Africa, Ukraine, Zambia and Zimbabwe were on the Red list, and have now moved to Orange)    All passengers from Red list countries must present negative results of a PCR or antigen test taken in the previous 48 hours at boarding and may be tested again on arrival. Unvaccinated passengers are subject to presentation of "compelling reasons" for travel, mandatory antigen testing on arrival, and must quarantine for 10 days under the control of security forces.     Passengers from Orange list countries must present negative results of a PCR or antigen test taken in the previous 48 hours at boarding. Vaccinated passengers are not subject to the "compelling reasons" regime, but unvaccinated people are and must commit to self-isolation lasting 7 days and undergo testing at the end of this period.     Although an Orange list country, additional regulations apply to all passengers aged 12 or over arriving from the United Kingdom from 14 January:     - All travelers, vaccinated or not, must present a negative test (PCR or antigen test) taken less than 24 hours before travel  - For vaccinated travellers, there is no longer any obligation to justify a compelling reason to come to France, nor an obligation to respect a period of isolation on arrival on the national territory. As such, the need to register, prior to travel, on the digital platform "eOS passenger" is lifted. Screenings on arrival may be conducted at the places of arrival. In the event of a positive result, the traveller will be placed in solitary confinement.  - For unvaccinated travellers, travel to or from the United Kingdom is permitted provided that it can prove compelling reasons valid for "red" countries.  - Unvaccinated travellers from the United Kingdom must continue to register, before their departure, on the eOS passenger digital platform, allowing them to enter the address of their stay in France. They must, upon arrival in France, observe a strict quarantine period of 10 days at this place; this quarantine will be controlled by law enforcement.    Specific guidance for UK passengers is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220117202519/https://www.gouvernement.fr/info-coronavirus/deplacements#voyager_dans_l'union_europeenne    Passengers from Green List countries are divided into two groups:     1. They may be tested for antigen on arrival.    2. Bahrain, Hong Kong, Japan, Kuwait, New Zealand, Qatar, Rwanda, Saudi Arabia, Senegal, South Korea, Taiwan, The United Arab Emirates, Uruguay and Vanuatu:  All travelers twelve years of age or older, regardless of their vaccination status,from these countries/territories must present for boarding, the negative result of a PCR test or an antigen test (TAG) carried out less than 48 hours before the flight. column60: From 24 January 2022, the "Health Pass" is replaced with the "Vaccine Pass" for everyone aged 16 and over.     To have the "vaccine pass", it is necessary to present one of these three proofs:    - A vaccination certificate attesting to a complete vaccination schedule, booster dose included within the time limit for people from 18 years and 1 month who are eligible.  - A certificate of recovery from Covid-19 dating back at least 11 days and less than 6 months.  - A certificate of medical contraindication that prevents vaccination. The persons concerned are thus issued by their doctor with a document that can be presented in the places, services, establishments and events where the "vaccination pass" is required.    People embarking on a vaccination journey until 15 February 2022 have the temporary opportunity to benefit from a valid "vaccination pass", provided they receive their second dose within 4 weeks and present a negative test of less than 24 hours.    The "vaccine pass" is required for:    - Access to places of leisure and culture (including performance halls, amusement parks, concert halls, festivals, sports halls, games halls, libraries and documentation centres, or cinemas);  - Commercial catering activities (bars and restaurants, including on terraces), with the exception of collective catering or take-away of prepared meals, professional road and rail catering, room service in hotel restaurants and bars and non-commercial catering, including the free distribution of meals;  - Trade fairs and exhibitions, and professional seminars if they take place outside the company and bring together more than 50 people;  - Long-distance travel by interregional public transport (domestic flights, TGV journeys, Intercités and night trains, interregional coaches);  - Ski lifts in ski resorts ;  - Access to tourist accommodation such as campsites or holiday clubs with a single control at the beginning of the stay.    Health and medico-social services and establishments, for persons accompanying or visiting persons accommodated in these services and establishments as well as for those who are welcomed there for scheduled care remain subject to the health pass, except emergency, and not to the vaccination pass.    These rules concerning the "vaccination pass" apply to customers and users of the establishments and activities concerned. It is the responsibility of operators to implement the "vaccine pass" in their establishments.    The vaccination pass is applicable to people and employees who intervene in these places, establishments, services or events, and are in contact with the public.    The "vaccination pass" does not apply to minors between the ages of 12 and 15. It is therefore the "health pass" - which includes the additional possibility of presenting proof of a negative test of less than 24 hours - which remains in force for this age group.    - https://web.archive.org/web/20220128203947/https://www.gouvernement.fr/info-coronavirus/pass-vaccinal

column29: From 4 February, the classification of countries from which travelers are subject to differentiated border controls based on health indicators is as follows:     - "Green" countries and territories: countries or territories in which no active circulation of the virus is observed and no variants of concern are identified. These are not all countries included in the lists of "green" and "red" countries.  - "Red" countries: countries in which active circulation of the virus is observed with the presence of variants of concern. To date, there are no countries classified as "red".  - "Scarlet red" countries: countries in which a particularly active circulation of the virus and the discovery of a variant likely to present a risk of increased transmissibility or immune escape are observed. To date, there is no country classified as "scarlet red".    Anyone aged 12 and over entering French territory must present a negative PCR or antigen test of less than 24 hours or 48 hours depending on the country of origin. column29: From 12 February, the classification of countries from which travelers are subject to differentiated border controls based on health indicators is as follows:     - "Green" countries and territories: countries or territories in which no active circulation of the virus is observed and no variants of concern are identified. These are the countries of the European area, to which are added Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, South Korea, the United Arab Emirates, Honduras, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Kuwait, New Zealand, Qatar, Rwanda, Senegal, Taiwan and Vanuatu.  - "Orange" countries: countries in which there is an active circulation of the virus in controlled proportions, without diffusion of worrying variants. These are not all countries included in the lists of "green" and "red" countries.  - "Red" countries: countries in which active circulation of the virus is observed with the presence of variants of concern. Currently, there are no countries classified as "red".  - "Scarlet red" countries: countries in which a particularly active circulation of the virus and the discovery of a variant likely to present a risk of increased transmissibility or immune escape are observed. Currently, there is no country classified as "scarlet red".    In orer to enter France, travelers must comply with rules specific to their country of departure:     1: travelers from a country/territory classified as "green"  - Travelers twelve years of age or older who do not have proof of a complete vaccination schedule or a certificate of recovery from Covid-19 must present before travel the negative result of a PCR test of less than 72 hours or antigenic test (TAG) of less than 48 hours.  - This obligation does not apply to the travel of road transport professionals in the exercise of their activity and to the following trips by land:  -- Journeys of less than 24 hours within a perimeter defined by a radius of 30 kilometres around the place of residence;  -- Business travel whose urgency or frequency is incompatible with the performance of a test or screening examination.    2: Travellers from a country/territory classified as "orange": all countries/territories other than those mentioned in paragraph 1 ("green")  Travelers twelve years of age or older who do not have proof of a complete vaccination schedule or a certificate of recovery from Covid-19 must present before travel the negative result of a PCR test of less than 72 hours or antigenic test (TAG) of less than 48 hours. They may be tested for antigen on arrival.    In addition:     - vaccinated travellers (full vaccination schedule) are not subject to the regime of compelling reasons.  - unvaccinated travellers are subject to the imperative grounds regime and will have to commit to a 7-day self-isolation and undergo a test at the end of this period. The list of compelling reasons is specified in the travel and travel certificate issued by the Ministry of the Interior. Under this list, the following may enter France: the French, their spouses and children, nationals of the European area as well as their spouses and children having their main residence in France or who join, in transit through France, their main residence in a country of the European area or the country of which they are nationals.    Whilst no countries are currently specified as Red or Scarlet Red, nnvaccinated travellers from these countries/territories would still be subject to the regime of compelling reasons for entering France, must present at boarding a negative result of a PCR test or an antigen test (TAG) carried out less than 48 hours before the flight, will be subject to a mandatory antigen test upon arrival, and would be subject to a mandatory 10-day quarantine,controlled by the security forces.     - https://web.archive.org/web/20220213064422/https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/informations-pratiques/article/coronavirus-covid-19     The specific rule requiring travelers from the United Kingdom to present results of a Covid-19 test taken within 24 hours of departure (rather than the usual 48 hours requires for travelers from other Orange list countries) has been rescinded as of 12 February. https://web.archive.org/web/20220213064422/https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/informations-pratiques/article/coronavirus-covid-19 and https://web.archive.org/web/20220221213430/https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/france/entry-requirements

column74: Vaccination is mandatory for all those who work in contact with frail people. Thus, since September 15, 2021, the following must be vaccinated:    - all staff (including administrative staff) of health institutions, medico-social institutions (EHPAD, USLD, autonomous residences, disability structures with or without accommodation and including non-medicalized), social institutions attached to a health institution (LHSS, LAM, CSAPA, CAARUD, CLAT, CEGGID);  - home helpers working with people affecting APA or PCH, in home services or as employees of individual employers;  - staff of medical transport companies (including taxis under agreement);  - all professions in Book IV of the CSP, whether or not under agreement, and professions for the use of titles, as well as their employees (e.g. medical secretaries, dental assistants);  - all health students;  - SDIS-Firefighters (professionals and volunteers);  - occupational health service personnel.    Persons justifying a contraindication to vaccination are exempt from the vaccination obligation.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220221071212/https://www.gouvernement.fr/info-coronavirus/vaccins

column29: On arrival, all passengers must take a compulsory test for COVID-19 at Libreville Airport at their own expense (CFA20,000). Passports will be retained by the immigration authorities during this time and returned after successful completion of the isolation time. If the COVID-19 test is negative, passengers will be able to leave quarantine and issued a test certificate, which is valid for 14 days and can be renewed at the end of this period after another test is undertaken. Holders of vaccination certificates still have to undergo the compulsory testing but can self-isolate in the facility of their choice and do not have to leave their passport. column29: Rules for non-vaccinated changed on 11 February, meaning that non-vaccinated people do not need to quarantine upon arrival in the UK. Rules as follows:    Fully vaccinated – from 11 February  If you qualify as fully vaccinated for travel to England, you:    will not need to take a COVID-19 test before you travel to England or after you arrive  will not need to quarantine when you arrive  You will need to complete a passenger locator form before you travel to England. column21: no policy change     Unless all passengers are members of the same family, a maximum of 3 persons are permitted to travel in a taxi or other private vehicle with up to 7 seats, or 4 persons in a private vehicle with up to 9 seats;  Cross-regional travel is allowed for mainland Greece and the islands of Lefkada, Evia and Salamina (use of self-tests ahead of travel is strongly recommended but is not mandatory).  Cross-regional travel to the rest of the islands is permitted but only with either:    proof of vaccination and 14 days since second dose (see Demonstrating your COVID-19 vaccination status), or  a negative result from a PCR test carried out up to 72 hours prior to travel; or  a negative result from a rapid test or self-test conducted up to 24 hours before travel; or  a self-test declaration signed less than 24 hours before travel; or  documentary proof of having recovered from Covid-19 (at least 2 months since infection, and no more than 9 months)  Travel in Greece  Travel within Greece between Regional Units is permitted subject to adherence to public health measures as outlined above. You must wear a mask at all times on all public transport.    If you are travelling via ferry, you will need to complete a health questionnaire and hand it to the ferry operator before boarding. The necessary forms will be provided by the operator: you should contact them directly if you need further information. Temperature checks may also be carried out before boarding.    If you are travelling by internal (domestic) flights, specific measures relating to check-in, baggage allowances and other details are in place to reduce the spread of coronavirus. You should check with your operator directly for further detail.  https://web.archive.org/web/20210802101710/https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/greece/coronavirus

column29: All those travelling to Greece (aged 5 or above) must show proof of a professionally administered negative rapid COVID-19 test taken no more than 24 hours before arrival or proof of a professionally administered negative PCR test taken no more than 72 hours before arrival.     The measure affects all arrivals, regardless of vaccination status or country of departure. The only exception is for arrivals who have spent less than 48 hours in a country prior to arriving in Greece.                                              Random antigen testing on arrival applies to every arrival to Greece, regardless of the certificate in their possession. If you are selected, please keep in mind that the screening is mandatory and in case of refusal, authorities reserve the right to refuse entry into the country.    If you are selected for a test and test positive, you will be subject to mandatory quarantine, for which you may be required by the Greek authorities to move to a designated quarantine facility.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220110161137/https://www.dfa.ie/travel/travel-advice/a-z-list-of-countries/greece/

column9: 22/3/22  Proof of Vaccination or Negative COVID Test Required for Most Businesses and Public Services:  As of Monday, November 22, 2021, the Government of Greece has restricted access for unvaccinated individuals to many categories of businesses and public services if they cannot prove vaccination or recovery from COVID-19.  Customers seeking access to these facilities are required to present a COVID-19 vaccination certificate or documentation of recovery from COVID-19.  Under the new rules, unvaccinated adults:  Cannot access/enter: Enclosed eating areas, entertainment facilities (cinemas, theaters), museums, exhibition centers, fitness centers and sports venues. These facilities may be accessed only by those who are fully vaccinated or have documentation of recovery from COVID-19.  Can enter only with a negative lab rapid test or PCR test: Unvaccinated individuals seeking access to churches, schools, public and private sector places of work, retail shops, hair salons, or outdoor eating areas may enter by presenting a negative laboratory rapid test no older than 48 hours OR a PCR test no older than 72 hours.  Can enter with no documentation required: Unvaccinated individuals can enter supermarkets, bakeries, sweet shops, pharmacies and urban public transportation.  Children aged 4 to 17 may access the top two categories of facilities with a negative self-test taken within the last 24 hours, documented via the Self-Test Declaration form. Children under four do not need to show any documentation.    Masks Still Required; Other Restrictions Still in Effect:  Greek authorities continue to enforce other restrictions to prevent the spread of COVID-19, including restrictions on certain business and entertainment operations, restrictions on the size of gatherings, and capacity limitations for public transport and businesses. As of December 24th at 6:00am masks are mandatory in all indoor spaces. As of March 5th, Greece will no longer require masks to be worn when outdoors, though masks are recommended in crowded, poorly ventilated areas and by the unvaccinated. Double mask or high protection-type (such as an N95) mask is required in supermarkets and on public transportation.  Additional information is available in English at travel.gov.gr and in Greek at the Civil Protection website and the Greek government’s COVID-19 Measures website.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220320124858/https://gr.usembassy.gov/covid-19-information/

column29: Conditions for entry into Greenland:  -To be permitted to enter Greenland, you must either be fully vaccinated or a resident of Greenland or you are relocating to Greenland.    -In regard to entering Greenland, you are considered fully vaccinated 14 days after you have completed a full vaccination programme, e.g. two doses of Pfizer or Moderna or one dose of Johnson&Johnson. There is currently no upper limit as to how long a person is considered fully vaccinated. This means that for the time being there is no requirement to get the booster vaccination to be considered fully vaccinated.    When you intend to travel to Greenland, you must remember to do the following:  -You must have a negative COVID-19 PCR test from a Nordic country (Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Iceland, Faroe Islands), UK, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, or a country in EU that is maximum 48 hours old from the time of departure and have valid documentation showing this.  -Bring a face mask for the journey and wear it during the journey, on the plane and in the airport, and also during transport to your place of residence. This rule applies to everyone at 12 years old or older.  https://web.archive.org/web/20211220215011/https://corona.nun.gl/en/travel/conditions-for-entry-into-greenland/

column15: In Greenland, there is a requirement that people aged 15 and older must be fully vaccinated if they want access to premises to which the public has access. Previously, a negative PCR test also gave access to such premises, but that is no longer possible.  -You must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19  -You are only allowed access to the following places if you are fully vaccinated against COVID-19:  1) Restaurants, cafes, pubs, discos and similar establishments.  2) Cultural institutions, including culture centres, cinemas, museums, exhibition halls, etc.  3) Community centres and similar establishments.  4) Libraries.  5) Indoor sports facilities, including sports colleges and sports halls, swimming pools, gyms, football pitches, etc.  6) Hairdressers, massage parlours, beauty clinics and similar establishments.  When are you fully vaccinated?  -People who have completed a full vaccination programme, for example two doses of Pfizer or Moderna vaccine or one dose of Johnson&Johnson vaccine, are considered fully vaccinated. There is currently no upper limit as to how long a person is considered fully vaccinated. This means that for the time being there is no requirement to get the booster vaccination to be considered fully vaccinated.  -If you have previously been infected with COVID-19 and can present documentation of a positive PCR test result which is between 14 days and 12 weeks old, you are covered by the same rules as if you were fully vaccinated.  *updated on 26Jan2022  https://web.archive.org/web/20211228235327/https://corona.nun.gl/en/corona-passport-digital-eu-covid-certificate/vaccination-as-a-requirement-for-access/

column29: 4th jan 2022  As part of Guam’s ongoing effort to contain the spread of COVID-19, individuals entering Guam by air or sea shall be subject to a 10-day quarantine, except as provided herein. Individuals who are fully vaccinated may be exempt from quarantine. Individuals are considered fully vaccinated 2 weeks after their second dose in a 2-dose series, or 2 weeks after a single-dose vaccine. Passengers who present a negative COVID-19 viral test may be exempt from quarantine. This guidance does not apply to individuals identified as close contacts to persons with COVID-19. Arriving passengers (air or sea) with direct flight/voyage into Guam that originate from a country with No Reported Cases are not required to have a COVID-19 test and are not required to quarantine  https://archive.fo/178N4    Non-vaccinated must provide negative test result and vaccinated present proof of vaccination.

Citizens of EU Member States (including Croatian citizens), i.e. Schengen Member States and Schengen associated countries, as well as members of their families and third-country nationals who are long-term residents under Council Directive 2003/109/EC of 25 November 2003 concerning the status of third-country nationals who are long-term residents and persons entitled to reside under other EU directives or national law or who have national long-term visas and are coming from third countries, must present a valid EU Digital COVID Certificate when entering the Republic of Croatia. Otherwise, it will not be accepted as credible for entering the Republic of Croatia.  certificate showing that they have recovered from COVID-19 and have received one dose of vaccine used in EU Member States (Pfizer, Moderna, AstaZeneca, Gamaleya, Sinopharm, Novavax, Janssen/Johnson&Johnson) or a vaccine approved by the World Health Organization for emergency use (Serum Institute of India - Covishield, Bharat Biotech - Covaxin, Sinovac - CoronaVac), provided that 14 days have passed since they received the single dose within eight months from contracting the disease, provided that the vaccine was administered less than 270 days from their arrival at the border crossing point;  positive PCR test result or rapid antigen test result, confirming that the holder recovered from the SARS-CoV-2 virus infection, which was performed in the previous 180 days and which is older than 11 days from the date of arrival at the border crossing point, or  a medical certificate of recovery;  or if they perform PCR testing or rapid antigen testing - RAT for SARS-CoV-2 immediately upon their arrival in the Republic of Croatia (at their own expense), with the obligation to stay in self-isolation until they obtain a negative test result. column29: English  This site contains information regarding the conditions of entry into the Republic of Croatia considering temporary bans, i.e. restrictions in place to prevent the spread of COVID-19.    If you cannot find the answer to your question, please contact us by filling in the form below.    Note: The necessary epidemiological measure of self-isolation is automatically determined for all passengers in transit, including personnel in the transport sector, if they do not leave the Republic of Croatia within 12 hours from the moment of entering the Republic of Croatia.     Passengers travelling to the Republic of Croatia from an EU / EEA member state    Passengers coming directly from the countries and/or regions of the European Union, i.e. countries and/or regions of the Schengen area and Schengen associated countries, regardless of their citizenship, will be allowed entry into the Republic of Croatia if they possess a valid EU Digital COVID Certificate.    Exceptionally, passengers arriving directly from the countries and/or regions of the European Union, i.e. countries and/or regions of the Schengen area and Schengen associated countries, who do not yet possess an EU Digital COVID Certificate, will be allowed entry into the Republic of Croatia if they have the following:     negative PCR test result or rapid antigen test result - RAT for SARS-CoV-2, where the RAT test must be listed in the Common list of rapid antigen tests recognized by the Member States of the European Union, published by the European Commission. If the RAT test results were made abroad, the manufacturer and/or the commercial name of the test must be visible. Otherwise, it will not be accepted as credible for entering the Republic of Croatia.  The PCR test result must not be older than 72 hours and the RAT test result must not be older than 24 hours, counting from the time the test was taken until the arrival at the border crossing point;   certificate that they have received two doses of vaccine used in the EU Member States (Pfizer, Moderna, AstaZeneca, Gamaleya, Sinopharm, Novavax) or vaccines approved by the World Health Organization for emergency use (Serum Institute of India - Covishield, Bharat Biotech - Covaxin, Sinovac - CoronaVac) not older than 270 days, provided that 14 days have passed since receiving the second dose of the vaccine, or a certificate that they have received one dose of the vaccine if the vaccine is administered in a single dose (Janssen/Johnson&Johnson) not older than 270 days, provided that 14 days have passed since they received the single dose, or a certificate that they have received the booster dose of the vaccine;  certificate showing that they have recovered from COVID-19 and have received one dose of vaccine used in EU Member States (Pfizer, Moderna, AstaZeneca, Gamaleya, Sinopharm, Novavax, Janssen/Johnson&Johnson) or a vaccine approved by the World Health Organization for emergency use (Serum Institute of India - Covishield, Bharat Biotech - Covaxin, Sinovac - CoronaVac), provided that 14 days have passed since they received the single dose within eight months from contracting the disease, provided that the vaccine was administered less than 270 days from their arrival at the border crossing point;   positive PCR test result or rapid antigen test result, confirming that the holder recovered from the SARS-CoV-2 virus infection, which was performed in the previous 180 days and which is older than 11 days from the date of arrival at the border crossing point, or  a medical certificate of recovery;  or if they perform PCR testing or rapid antigen testing - RAT for SARS-CoV-2 immediately upon their arrival in the Republic of Croatia (at their own expense), with the obligation to stay in self-isolation until they obtain a negative test result. In case they cannot get tested, they have to self-isolate for seven (7) days.    The following categories are exempt from possessing a valid EU Digital COVID Certificate or from the abovementioned obligations:     workers or self-employed persons performing essential tasks, including healthcare workers, frontier and posted workers and seasonal workers as specified in the Guidelines concerning  the exercise of the free movement of workers during COVID-19 outbreak;  pupils, students and interns  seafarers and workers in the transport sector or transport service providers, including heavy goods vehicle drivers transporting goods to be used in the national territory and those in transit only;  diplomats, staff of international organizations and persons invited by international organizations and whose physical presence is necessary for the functioning of those organizations, military personnel and police officers, as well as humanitarian and civil protection personnel in the performance of their duties;  persons traveling for family or business reasons, including journalists in the performance of their duties;  passengers in transit with the obligation to leave the Republic of Croatia within 12 hours from entry;  patients traveling for health reasons.    The provisions regarding frontier workers apply adequately to other categories of passengers who, due to the nature of their job or occupation, need to cross the state border frequently (e.g. athletes playing for clubs in a neighbouring country). column45: No contact tracing scheme officially announced.   Sources: https://archive.vn/3JHc5; https://archive.vn/b7O87.  But there is mobile contact tracing app - VirusRadar. Hungary launched VirusRadar mobile contact tracing application donated by Nextsense.   VirusRadar mobile application uses Nextsense Contact Tracing Technology for the detection of potentially exposed persons to Covid-19, implemented in StopKorona! mobile app. This mobile app for Apple iOS and Android implements the highest security standards, provides full control over personal data, and guarantees privacy protection. column27: The government continues to try to suppress the import of COVID-19 cases, especially the Omicron variant. The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column9: National overview as of 19 Jan: No nationwide school closure or student vaccine mandate has been imposed by the national govt (“Union govt”/”Centre”). However, several state governments have enacted school closures and other restrictions. While some areas (i.e Tamil Nadu) have enacted vaccine-differentiated restrictions, restrictions in many areas apply regardless of vaccination status.    Coding explanation: Unvaccinated and vaccinated are both coded 3G, to reflect the widespread closures found in at least *29* states/union territories, encompassing several of the most highly-populated regions. Note that vaccine-differentiated policies do exist, but states with such policies (I.e Tamil Nadu) have not yet opened schools for anyone, though it is planned to do so soon (1 Feb, for Tamil Nadu). Therefore, the coding is 3G to reflect how closure for vaccinated and unvaccinated is effectively the same for the time being, due to the same type of restriction (i.e physical closure of schools for everyone regardless of vaccination status). column12: Important note: Addition of vaccine-differentiated coding from this point.     1.	This indicator codes for physical closures/modified workplace requirements. (Example: Total closure of workplace, work-from-home requirements, orders to operate at 50% capacity instead).     2.	Additionally, vaccine-differentiation coding for this indicator records for requirements for visitors/customers to be vaccinated, *not staff/employees.* (Example: “Customers must show proof of vaccination to dine at a restaurant.”)    3.	For vaccine-differentiated measures for *staff/employees of workplaces*, please see indicator *V4* (Vaccine Mandates) instead. (Example: “Mandatory vaccination for restaurant staff.”)     National overview for 19-31 Jan: No nationwide workplace closures or vaccine mandates have been imposed by the national government. However, state governments have imposed workplace restrictions of varying stringency. Some, but not all, measures are vaccine-differentiated.     A. Non-vaccine differentiated measures:     1. column29: For the period of 18—21 January, the protocol for international travellers emphasises differentiation mainly regarding whether the traveller is from an "At Risk" country or not, rather than vaccination status.     1. Screening:   - Regardless of vaccination status, all travellers must have a negative result on their PCR test no more than 72 hours before departure. Travellers must also complete and submit a declaration form on the Air Suvidha Portal.   - Upon arrival, travellers from "Countries Specified At Risk" must take a PCR test and may not leave the airport until they receive their result.  - Travellers who are not from such countries do not ordinarily need to be tested, but PCR tests are carried out on a random sample (2%) of this group.     2. Quarantine: All travellers, regardless of vaccination status and country of origin, must quarantine for 7 days. It is not possible to "test out" of quarantine, even if one tests negative on PCR test taken at the airport.     3. Screening: A final PCR test is required on Day 8, with the result uploaded on the Air Suvidha Portal.    Archived sources:  1. column55: No policy change. Government continues to allocate funds for vaccine, universally available for individuals 15 years and older. However, noted that recently announced Indian national budget (on 1 Feb) had much lower allocation for vaccination compared to previous year; possibility of future booster shots having less or no government funding unless further funds are allocated.    “The proposal of Rs 5,000 crore Covid-19 vaccination Budget for this year hints that the Centre has done its job of providing free vaccines across the country and people may have to shell out for booster shots, according to experts. For 2021-22, the actual budget for Covid-19 vaccination was pegged at Rs 35,000 crore, which was later revised to Rs 39,000 crore. This year, the budget has been pared down to Rs 5,000 as India is on the verge of vaccinating the majority of its population.”    Source: 1. https://web.archive.org/web/20220207222858/https://www.news18.com/news/india/govt-slashing-covid-vaccination-budget-for-2022-could-mean-people-buying-booster-dose-on-their-own-say-experts-4725005.html

column18: As of March 1, the measures in place or planned in the following states or union territories are:    Andaman and Nicobar: An overnight 21:00-05:00 curfew is no longer active. Officials have lifted restrictions on tourist spots, other establishments, private vehicles, and gatherings. Public transport may operate at 75 percent capacity. Domestic travelers must hold negative results of a COVID-19 test taken within 48 hours before departure or vaccination certificates. Unvaccinated domestic travelers without pre-departure test results, as well as all entrants with an overseas travel history in the past 30 days, must take an on-arrival PCR test and quarantine until they receive a negative test result. Additional entry, testing, and quarantine rules are likely to enter tribal areas in the Nicobar Islands.    Andhra Pradesh: The 23:00-05:00 nightly curfew is no longer in place. Outdoor and indoor gatherings are capped at 200 and 100 people, respectively. Domestic arrivals must register online up to 72 hours before travel on the Andhra Pradesh police website. Domestic entrants do not require proof of vaccination or pre-departure testing; officials may direct symptomatic arrivals to undergo testing and/or quarantine based on test results.    Karnataka: Demonstrations are banned; permitted gatherings must be limited to 300 people if outdoors, and 200 people if indoors. Most in-person educational classes have resumed. Most venues, including state government offices, as well as dine-in, some recreational, and most sports facilities, may function at full capacity. Only fully vaccinated people can use dine-in, recreational, religious, and sports venues. Checkpoints and interstate transport curbs are most likely in border areas of Belagavi, Chamarajanagar, Dakshina Kannada, Kodagu, and Mysuru districts. Domestic arrivals must register online up to 72 hours before travel. Officials require entrants from Kerala, Goa, and Maharashtra states to provide a vaccine certificate.    Kerala: All arrivals must register online via the Jagratha portal up to 72 hours before travel. Unvaccinated entrants without pre-departure test results must take an on-arrival test and quarantine at home until they test negative or undergo a 14-day home quarantine. Pre-approved domestic travelers leaving the state within seven days are exempt from quarantine. On-arrival testing is limited to symptomatic and randomly selected international travelers. All international entrants are advised to self-monitor their health, submit to symptom surveillance, as well as avoid gatherings and crowded places for seven days from their arrival.    Puducherry: Large public gatherings remain prohibited through March 31, except permitted events such as funerals and weddings. Commercial, educational, and recreational venues, as well as transport services, can operate at full capacity. Retail outlets must ensure employees are vaccinated. Domestic entrants do not require proof of vaccination or pre-departure testing; officials may direct symptomatic arrivals to undergo testing and/or quarantine based on test results.    Tamil Nadu: All in-person educational classes have resumed statewide. Officials have lifted capacity limits on public transport as well as dine-in, grooming, sports, and retail venues. Staff at customer-facing positions and passengers on local suburban trains must be vaccinated. Public gatherings remain banned except for permitted events. Guest limits for weddings and funerals are 200 and 100, respectively. All domestic travelers must register online beforehand; those from Kerala must also carry proof of vaccination or negative pre-departure test results. Interstate travel curbs are possible, mainly to and from Kerala State.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220314103918/https://crisis24.garda.com/alerts/2022/02/india-kerala-state-lifts-most-covid-19-curbs-as-of-march-1-update-47

column18: Family and social gatherings  People should limit their contacts throughout the coming period to the greatest degree possible and visits to private homes should be kept to a maximum of 3 other households (that is, 4 households in total).    Hospitality  All restaurants, bars and cafes, excluding take away or delivery services, close at 8pm. This also applies to hotel restaurants and bars, except for overnight residents.    Strict social distancing is required in all bars and restaurants, including hotels (reverting to pre-22 October measures):    COVID pass required  table service only (no counter service)  1 metre between tables  maximum 6 adults per table (maximum 15 persons when including children aged 12 and younger)  no multiple table bookings and no intermingling  masks when not seated at table  Nightclubs are closed.    You may be asked for contact tracing data (for example: name, contact number).    Indoor events  No indoor events, including entertainment, cultural, community and sporting events, will take place after 8pm. In relation to events happening earlier in the day, attendance should be limited to 50% of venue capacity or 1,000 attendees, whichever is the lower. This includes cinemas. This does not affect religious, educational or normal workplace business activity and business events (for example: conferences, trade fairs).    You may be asked for contact tracing data (for example: name, contact number).    Wedding receptions can take place with a capacity limit of 100 guests and continue after 8pm. Midnight closing time still applies.    Religious services  Religious services can proceed without capacity limits but with all other protective measures remaining in place.    Outdoor events  Attendance at outdoor events, including entertainment, cultural, community and sporting events, should be limited to 50% of venue capacity or 5,000 attendees, whichever is the lower.    Group activities  Organisers of indoor and outdoor group activities should ensure that appropriate protective measures are in place, and where indoor groups have a mix of vaccinated and unvaccinated people indoors, pods of 6 should apply.    For children under 18, the “pod of 6” system can be adjusted to allow for indoor games and competition activities only, with all other protective measures remaining in place.    The “pod of 6” system should be retained for all other settings such as training activities and games as part of training. Fixed capacity limits will not apply to these indoor and outdoor group activities.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220121175253/https://www.gov.ie/en/publication/3361b-public-health-updates/

Protect yourself and others from COVID-19    If you have any symptoms of COVID-19, even mild ones, you should:    - self-isolate (stay in your room) until 48 hours after your symptoms are mostly or fully gone  - wear a face mask if you have to be around other people    Do these even if you completed your first round of COVID-19 vaccination, had a booster, or had COVID-19 in the past.    Do    - get a COVID-19 vaccine and booster dose when it's available to you    - keep at least 2 metres (around 6 feet) away from people you do not live with    - wash your hands properly and often    - wear a face mask in crowded places outdoors and when you move around in public indoor spaces    - cover coughs or sneezes with a tissue or your sleeve - put used tissues into a bin and wash your hands    - meet people outdoors where possible    - try to avoid crowded places where you cannot keep a distance from people - there's a greater risk of infection in crowded and enclosed places    - check that visitors to your home or workplace do not have symptoms of COVID-19, colds or flu    - let fresh air into your home by opening windows, doors and air vents as much as possible when you have visitors    - clean objects and surfaces that other people touch      Don't    - do not touch your eyes, nose or mouth if your hands are not clean    - do not share objects that touch your mouth, for example, bottles or cups    - do not shake hands or make close contact with other people, if possible    - do not wear gloves instead of washing your hands - your hands can get contaminated when you take them off      https://web.archive.org/web/20220319141023/https://www2.hse.ie/conditions/covid19/preventing-the-spread/protect-yourself-and-others/

column55: 11th April 2022, Getting a booster dose    To get your first booster dose, you must be aged 12 or older.    12 to 15 year olds must attend their booster appointment with a parent or legal guardian. A parent or legal guardian will need to give consent for their child's vaccination.    Do not book an appointment for a second booster dose yet. These will be available soon for:    people over 65  people over 12 with a weak immune system  How long to wait before getting your first booster    After your first round of COVID-19 vaccination, you need to wait:    3 months (at least 90 days) if you are 16 or older  6 months (at least 182 days) if you are aged 12 to 15  You will not get your booster dose if the minimum interval has not passed on the day of your appointment.    If you had COVID-19 since you were vaccinated, you should get your booster dose at least:    3 months after your positive test result or when symptoms started if you are 16 or older  6 months after your positive test result or when symptoms started if you are aged 12 to 15  If you had an additional dose because you have a weak immune system, you can get your booster at least 3 months after your additional dose if you are 12 or older.    Vaccines:    Pfizer/BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine  Moderna/Spikevax COVID-19 vaccine  Novavax COVID-19 vaccine  Janssen COVID-19 vaccine  AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine (not currently available)    https://web.archive.org/web/20220412001307/https://covid19booster.healthservice.ie/hse-self-referral/?flow=booster

As of Dec,27,2021, Iranian authorities have banned travellers from additional four countries: Denmark, France, Norway and the UK from entering the country through at least January,08 due to concerns over the COVID-19 Omicron variant. Officials have also extended the ban on travellers from Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe through Jan,08. Iranian nationals returning from these countries can enter but must take two PCR tests and produce negative results on both or quarantine for up to 14 days. Authorities have closed all land borders through at least January,08. Travellers over the age of two must present a negative result from a PCR test taken within 72 hours before departure in order to gain entry. Foreign national who do not have a negative PCR test will be denied entry. Iranian nationals, regardless of vaccination status, can enter Iran. Foreign travellers must provide a double-vaccination certificate issued at least two weeks prior to travel to Iran. Iranian nationals without a vaccine certificate must undergo a PCR test and quarantine at designated isolation centres. Travellers who exhibit symptoms of the disease will be subject to a two week quarantine period at government-approved centres. Travellers who receive a negative PCR test result before leaving Iran are not required to provide a new one if they return within two weeks. column32: Key measures of the 2020 package included (i) extra funding for the health sector (2 percent of GDP); (ii) cash transfers to vulnerable households (0.5 percent of GDP); (iii) support to the unemployment insurance fund (0.3 percent of GDP); and (iv) subsidized loans for affected businesses and vulnerable households (4.7 percent of GDP).
