column9: From FB page of Office of Te Beretitenti (date of post was 19/02/22 but post refers to policy measures introduced on 18/02/22)    Targeted measure: "8. School closure until the end of this month."    "Government has decided to further extend the lockdown period on the islands of North Tarawa, Maiana, Abaiang, Marakei and Abemama for another two more weeks or may be longer should the need arise and with different conditions due to the slow in spread of the diseases on these islands, effective from Friday 18th of February 2022. The islands of Aranuka and Makin who have just affected with the spread of COVID-19 will also be included among these islands.    Subsequent to the decision pertaining to this extension, there are also new decisions put in place in addition to the current measures under the Alert Level 3. These new measures which will only apply on North Tarawa, Maiana, Abaiang, Marakei and Abemama, including  Aranuka and Makin are as follows:  1. Curfew hours from 6pm to 6am everyday.   2. All Government Offices and SOES will be closed and work remotely from home, except for essential and emergency services which also follow the Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS) guidelines:  ? Island Council Office  ? Hospital services  ? Police services  ? Kiribati Oil Company and gas stations  ? Wholesalers and retailers selling food  ? Telecommunication service providers  ? Kiribati Red Cross Society  ? Kiribati Family Health Association  3. And other essential that the Government and the Island Council deems necessary during the curfew. These additional services require prior approval of the Island Council Office.  4. All essential service providers (food wholesale and retail) from the private sector will remain open to the public from 6am to 6pm.  5. People MUST stay at home – may only leave their homes for essential work, or to access emergency services but must observe compulsory face mask, social distancing of 2 meters, not spitting and nose blowing in public places and other guidelines from the Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS).  6. Access to shops for food shopping and other essential services will be zoned to limit the movement of people within their neighborhoods or villages from 6am to 6pm.  7. Public transportation services may operate but will also observe compulsory face mask, open windows, no spitting and nose blowing, and other MHMS guidelines and passengers must not share seats nor stand.  8. School closure until the end of this month.  9. All kava bars, liquor bars, and night clubs will be closed  10. Social gatherings (including Churches) up to 20 people are allowed to gather in outdoor setting. With appropriate distance, masks and good ventilation.  11. Access to hospital services will be conducted accordingly to the Ministry of Health and Medical Services guidelines as earlier announced.  12. Delivery of cargoes , fuels and medical supplies by vessels or air services will continue to outer island with no passengers allowed. Only those stranded in the outer islands are allowed to return to Tarawa provided they meet health travel requirements.  13. No travels between the outer islands are allowed.  14. All police officers and other responsible Government officers are hereby ordered to ensure that this Order and future directions issued out of this Order and Public Health (Infectious Disease) Regulation and the Disaster Risk Management and Climate Change Act are complied with by the public.   15. Urgent direction(s) other than those listed here, if there is a need, may be issued later to the police and other officers of the Government for execution in relation to certain areas or groups of people or activities etc where it deemed necessary to achieve the purposes of this Order and the Public Health (Infectious Disease) Regulation and the Disaster Risk Management and Climate Change Act in relation to COVID-19.  16. Any person who contravenes any conditions of this Order commits an offence and will be liable to be arrested by the police or imprisonment. For clarification purposes, any breach of all the provisions of the Public Health (Infectious Disease) Regulation is an offence.  17. In case of any inconsistencies between this version and the Kiribati version, the Kiribati version shall prevail.  18. This Order repeals any previous Order and is effective on 18th February 2022 at 6 am until 4th March 2022 at 6am.  19. The non-affected islands with COVID-19 will continue their operations as usual.    Any person who contravenes any conditions of this Order commits an offence and will be liable to be arrested by the police or imprisonment. For clarification purposes, any breach of all the provisions of the Public Health (Infectious Disease) Regulation is an offence.   In case of any inconsistencies between this version and the Kiribati version, the Kiribati version shall prevail.    The public is advised to continue to strictly follow the Ministry of Health and Medical Services Standard Operational Procedures, comply with the curfew order, and to visit clinics for test if receiving symptoms to safeguard themselves and their families from this pandemic.    http://archive.today/7Q8G0

column29: The Kuwaiti government is currently imposing a seven-day COVID-19-related quarantine period at home or in a hotel for all arriving international travellers. This marks a reduction from the previously implemented 10-day quarantine period. Vaccinated travellers can end the quarantine earlier if a PCR test taken on arrival proves negative. Returning Kuwaiti citizens who are not fully inoculated must undergo a seven-day institutional quarantine period. Vaccinated Kuwaiti nationals are required to undergo seven days of home quarantine.  A ban on travel from Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Zambia, and Zimbabwe is in place until further notice. Kuwaiti citizens returning from these countries will be subject to a seven-day mandatory quarantine. Foreign nationals must spend 14 days in a third country before they can enter Kuwait.  https://archive.ph/v0pDb

column29: International Travel Restrictions  The government continues to suspend tourist visas, visas on arrival, and standing visa exemptions from most international locations. Government agencies or other entities may apply for entry approval for foreign essential workers, technical experts, and investors. International entrants must obtain prior permission from Lao authorities at least seven days before arrival; provide a valid entry visa if applicable, a negative result from a PCR test taken within 72 hours before departure, and a completed health declaration form; and download the LaoKYC application. Foreign nationals must also have insurance coverage for COVID-19 treatment and other related expenses from international or local providers.    Authorities allow tourist arrivals from several locations in the first phase of Green Travel Zone international travel reopening scheme through March 31. The locations include Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brunei, Cambodia, Canada, China, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Malaysia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Philippines, Poland, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, Switzerland, the US, the UK, Thailand, and Vietnam. Travelers must be fully vaccinated at least 14 days before arrival, have a health insurance policy with a coverage of at least USD 50,000, obtain a negative PCR test result taken within 72 hours before departure, undergo an on-arrival PCR test, and remain at their accommodation for 48 hours until they receive a negative result from the on-arrival test.    In the first phase of reopening, officials allow tourists to visit the Green Travel Zones of Vientiane Capital, Luang Prabang Province, and Vang Vieng District of Vientiane Province, as well as the Green Travel Trails of Champasack, Khammouane, Oudomxay, Xayaboury, and Xieng Khouang provinces. Green Travel Zones and Green Travel Trails are areas with vaccination rates of at least 70 percent and below 70 percent respectively. Authorities permit tourists to enter only through Wattay International Airport (VTE) and the First Lao-Thai Friendship Bridge in Vientiane Prefecture. Officials plan to categorize other localities, including Savannakhet Province, as Green Travel Zones and Green Travel Trails areas, and announce additional points of entry in the second phase of reopening from April 1-June 30.    Officials allow some border checkpoints, including those with Thailand, to open. column29: 28/1/22  Travelers coming from Libya must abide by the same requirements as other international travelers, as listed below.  International travelers aged 12 and over a must present a negative COVID-19 PCR Test within 48 hours of their flight to Tunisia. Vaccinated individuals are no longer exempt from the testing requirement.  Unvaccinated travelers, or travelers who are not fully vaccinated, must complete a seven-day mandatory quarantine at a government-approved hotel. Upon entry to Tunisia, these travelers must present a reservation receipt proving their intent to comply with this requirement. Please find the list of government-approved hotels here. Travelers must obtain a COVID-19 PCR Test between the fifth and seventh day of the quarantine.  Fully vaccinated travelers are exempt from the mandatory seven-day quarantine at a government-approved hotel upon presentation of their official vaccination card.  Travelers should be advised that they will be required to comply with all PCR and COVID-19 testing and quarantine requirements in Tunisia.  Travelers are further advised to carefully review guidance from Tunisian Ministry of Health authorities.  https://web.archive.org/web/20220128151935/https://ly.usembassy.gov/u-s-citizen-services/covid-19-information/

Gatherings of between 21 and 200 people (inclusive) are subject to the CovidCheck 2G+ system, or the requirement to wear a mask and be seated at a minimum distance of 2 metres. column32: The authorities have created a special fund dedicated to the management of the pandemic, of about 3 percent of GDP financed by the government and by voluntary contributions from public and private entities which will be tax deductible. This fund covers the costs of upgrading medical facilities and support businesses and households impacted by the pandemic. Businesses with less than 500 employees made temporarily idle and experiencing a reduction in turnover of more than 50 percent were authorized to defer social contribution payments until June 30. Their employees who become temporarily unemployed and are registered with the pension fund received 2,000 dirhams a month and were allowed put off debt payments until June 30. In April, 2020 almost 1 million workers from 134,000 companies were eligible to these transfers. Companies and households can also defer income tax payment until September 30, 2020. In addition, the government has decided to accelerate payment to its suppliers to support businesses. The government has extended social transfers to employees temporarily unemployed and further deferred social contribution payments for some sectors (including tourism) until end-March 2021.    The government also took measures to support households working in the informal sector. Households’ benefiting from the non-contributory health insurance (RAMED) received a monthly mobile payment of DRH 800-1200 (USD 80-120) from April, depending on households’ composition. Other households which do not benefit from RAMED can claim cash support by registering online. In April, 85 percent of eligible households in the informal sectoral were covered. The government postponed the deadline for personal income tax filing from end-April to end-June 2020 and provided a tax exemption for additional compensation paid by firms to employees in the formal sector up to a limit of 50 percent of the average monthly net salary. A decree-law adopted on April 6, 2020 authorizes the government to increase external borrowing beyond the ceiling approved in the 2020 Budget Act.    On August 6,2020 the authorities announced a plan to sustain the economic recovery and employment levels. The plan envisages the mobilization of DRH 120 billion, mainly in the form of credit guarantees to firms and funding for a newly -created “Fund for Strategic Investment”, which will finance investment projects (including PPPs) and sustain the capital of firms that needs equity injections to develop their business.    https://web.archive.org/web/20211022120614/https://www.imf.org/en/Topics/imf-and-covid19/Policy-Responses-to-COVID-19#M

column32: The authorities have created a special fund dedicated to the management of the pandemic, of about 3 percent of GDP financed by the government and by voluntary contributions from public and private entities which will be tax deductible. This fund covers the costs of upgrading medical facilities and support businesses and households impacted by the pandemic. Businesses with less than 500 employees made temporarily idle and experiencing a reduction in turnover of more than 50 percent were authorized to defer social contribution payments until June 30. Their employees who become temporarily unemployed and are registered with the pension fund received 2,000 dirhams a month and were allowed put off debt payments until June 30. In April, 2020 almost 1 million workers from 134,000 companies were eligible to these transfers. Companies and households can also defer income tax payment until September 30, 2020. In addition, the government has decided to accelerate payment to its suppliers to support businesses. The government has extended social transfers to employees temporarily unemployed and further deferred social contribution payments for some sectors (including tourism) until end-March 2021.    The government also took measures to support households working in the informal sector. Households’ benefiting from the non-contributory health insurance (RAMED) received a monthly mobile payment of DRH 800-1200 (USD 80-120) from April, depending on households’ composition. Other households which do not benefit from RAMED can claim cash support by registering online. In April, 85 percent of eligible households in the informal sectoral were covered. The government postponed the deadline for personal income tax filing from end-April to end-June 2020 and provided a tax exemption for additional compensation paid by firms to employees in the formal sector up to a limit of 50 percent of the average monthly net salary. A decree-law adopted on April 6, 2020 authorizes the government to increase external borrowing beyond the ceiling approved in the 2020 Budget Act.    On August 6,2020 the authorities announced a plan to sustain the economic recovery and employment levels. The plan envisages the mobilization of DRH 120 billion, mainly in the form of credit guarantees to firms and funding for a newly -created “Fund for Strategic Investment”, which will finance investment projects (including PPPs) and sustain the capital of firms that needs equity injections to develop their business.    https://web.archive.org/web/20211022120614/https://www.imf.org/en/Topics/imf-and-covid19/Policy-Responses-to-COVID-19#M

column15: Moldovan authorities established new public health measures to limit the spread of COVID-19 infection at all public events and gatherings, both indoor and outdoor.  Anyone over the age of 18 eating in a restaurant or café or attending any show, concert, festival, theater, cinema, concert hall, nightclub, dance floor, etc., must present one of the following documents: 1) a negative PCR COVID-19 test (taken in the last 72 hours) or an antigen test (taken in the last 48 hours); 2) a COVID-19 vaccine certificate (valid 14 days after the second dose); 3) a medical certificate attesting the person had COVID-19 in the previous 6 months; 4) a COVID-19 antibodies certificate valid for 90 days from the exam date. column29: No entry bans from any country. The following rules applied to over 50 countries until January 17th and applies to all countries since then: Moldova requires anyone entering the country present one of the following:  1) a COVID-19 vaccine certificate (valid 14 days after the second dose); 2) a negative PCR COVID-19 test (taken in the last 72 hours) or an antigen test (taken in the last 48 hours); 3) a medical certificate attesting the person had COVID-19 in the previous 6 months; or 4) a COVID-19 antibodies certificate valid for 90 days from the exam date.  Any COVID-19 antibodies certificate or evidence of vaccination must be in Romanian, English, French, German, Italian, or Russian language.  Moldovan Border Police accept all types of vaccination with appropriate documentation.  Absent one of the documents listed above, a traveler will have to self-isolate for 14 days.  Self-isolation may be discontinued after 7 days if a COVID-19 PCR test or a rapid SARS-CoV-2 Ag test is performed, and the result is negative based on a confirmative document.  If you are subject to self-isolation and depart Moldova, you could be fined for violating self-isolation.  Anyone required to self-isolate should complete an online epidemiological card 3 days before arriving in Moldova.  https://web.archive.org/web/20220125001334/https://md.usembassy.gov/u-s-citizen-services/covid-19-information/  https://web.archive.org/web/20220107182222/https://msmps.gov.md/comunicare/lista-statelor-cu-risc-epidemiologic-sporit-de-transmitere-a-infectiei-covid-l9-2/

column29: Effective January 17, 2022, Moldova requires anyone entering the country present one of the following:  1) a COVID-19 vaccine certificate (valid 14 days after the second dose); 2) a negative PCR COVID-19 test (taken in the last 72 hours) or an antigen test (taken in the last 48 hours); 3) a medical certificate attesting the person had COVID-19 in the previous 6 months; or 4) a COVID-19 antibodies certificate valid for 90 days from the exam date.  Any COVID-19 antibodies certificate or evidence of vaccination must be in Romanian, English, French, German, Italian, or Russian language.  Moldovan Border Police accept all types of vaccination with appropriate documentation.  Absent one of the documents listed above, a traveler will have to self-isolate for 14 days.  Self-isolation may be discontinued after 7 days if a COVID-19 PCR test or a rapid SARS-CoV-2 Ag test is performed, and the result is negative based on a confirmative document.  If you are subject to self-isolation and depart Moldova, you could be fined for violating self-isolation.  Anyone required to self-isolate should complete an online epidemiological card 3 days before arriving in Moldova.  Exceptions to the entry rules above are made for the following categories of persons if they do not show clinical signs of respiratory infection or fever:  1) children up to 12 years of age; 2) students up to 18 years age going to study or travel for activities related to completing/ organizing/conducting/ participating in international competitions; 3) persons travelling for health reasons, including accompanying persons with appropriate documentation; 4) passengers in transit (24 hours transiting Moldova), the transit itinerary to be established by the Border Police; 4) persons who are summoned by courts/law enforcement as well as their legal representatives with appropriate documentation; 5) holders of diplomatic, service, official and special passports, as well as holders of Laissez-Passer travel documents issued by the United Nations, including family members of diplomatic and consular missions, and international organizations/missions accredited to the Republic of Moldova.  https://web.archive.org/web/20220313200703/https://md.usembassy.gov/u-s-citizen-services/covid-19-information/

column29: """To enter Madagascar you will need to provide proof of a negative PCR test taken within 72 hours of travel.     You will also be required to make an advance hotel booking for two nights and pay in advance for at least one night for quarantine after your arrival, and take a COVID-19 test on arrival at Ivato International Airport. The €25 cost of the test can be paid in cash or by bank card on arrival. You will be asked to complete a declaration to confirm you will abide by quarantine until the result of your arrival test, and a locator form to indicate your movements after quarantine. If the test is negative, you will be able to leave quarantine within 24-48hrs. If the test is positive, you will need to quarantine for a further 14 days and may be referred to a local medical facility for treatment if you develop serious symptoms. Quarantine and medical treatment costs are at your own expense, so you should check what your insurance covers in advance of travel.""  https://web.archive.org/web/20220308083315/https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/madagascar/entry-requirements"

column29: """To enter Madagascar you will need to provide proof of a negative PCR test taken within 72 hours of travel.     You will also be required to make an advance hotel booking for two nights and pay in advance for at least one night for quarantine after your arrival, and take a COVID-19 test on arrival at Ivato International Airport. The €25 cost of the test can be paid in cash or by bank card on arrival. You will be asked to complete a declaration to confirm you will abide by quarantine until the result of your arrival test, and a locator form to indicate your movements after quarantine. If the test is negative, you will be able to leave quarantine within 24-48hrs. If the test is positive, you will need to quarantine for a further 14 days and may be referred to a local medical facility for treatment if you develop serious symptoms. Quarantine and medical treatment costs are at your own expense, so you should check what your insurance covers in advance of travel.""  https://web.archive.org/web/20220308083315/https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/madagascar/entry-requirements"

column12: As of January 17th, only fully vaccinated people are allowed to access the following facilities: Bars, Clubs, Restaurants, Snack Bars, Cinemas, Theatres, Casinos, Gambling Halls, Bingo Parlours, Sporting Events, Gyms, Fitness Centres, Public Pools, Spas and Saunas, Organized Events and Exhibitions. Vaccination status is verified at the establishment via QR Code (via CovPass - Malta App), or recognized foreign certificates.  Exemptions from vaccination requirement include: those aged less than 12, those who are pregnant, those with a recent positive result, and those with certain recognized medical conditions. Employees of such establishments who interact directly with customers must be vaccinated by February 1st, 2022 (those who don't directly interact with customers are exempt from the vaccination requirement).    Additional measures are also implemented, including temperature, sanitizing stations, maintaining patron contact information for 28 days, mandatory masking (exemption for boosted groups of 1-2), socially distanced seating.    Therefore, interpreted as a closure of all but essential services to those who are non-vaccinated, and a recommended closing to those who are vaccinated, given the maintenance of some social distancing measures.    Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20220116073055/https://deputyprimeminister.gov.mt/en/health-promotion/covid-19/Documents/mitigation-conditions-and-guidances/Standards-for-entry-to-establishments-and-events_13Jan22.pdf     http://web.archive.org/web/20220117104926/https://www.maltatoday.com.mt/news/national/114358/masks_no_longer_mandatory_for_those_with_a_booster_dose_from_monday#.YeVJwZr7RkU
column15: As of January 17th, proof of vaccination is required to attend organized events, namely: events including cultural, artistic, dance, theatre, music performances, etc., corporate events - conferences, awards nights, AGMs, etc., fairs, markets, and exhibitions, weddings and other celebrations and to spectate at sports events. Vaccination status is verified at the establishment via QR Code (via CovPass - Malta App), or recognized foreign certificates.  Exemptions from vaccination requirements include those aged less than 12, those who are pregnant, those with a recent positive result, and those with certain recognized medical conditions. Employees of event venues who interact directly with customers must be vaccinated by February 1st, 2022 (those who don't directly interact with customers are exempt from the vaccination requirement).    Additional measures are also implemented, including temperature screening, sanitizing stations, requiring pre-registration/ticket purchasing (no ticket sales at the door), mandatory masking, socially distanced seating (no standing events), mandatory maintenance of patron contact information for 28 days, staggered entrance/exit times, and events must be pre-approved and may be inspected.    Therefore, interpreted as a closure of public events to those who are non-vaccinated, and a recommended closing to those who are vaccinated, given the maintenance of some social distancing measures.    https://deputyprimeminister.gov.mt/en/health-promotion/covid-19/Documents/mitigation-conditions-and-guidances/Organised-Safe-Events_17Jan22.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20220322071024/https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/malta-roll-back-vaccine-certificate-requirements-february-2022-01-25/  https://web.archive.org/web/20220322071041/https://www.conventionsmalta.com/en-GB/news/%20airportreopeningfully/2131

13/02/22    YANGON, Nov. 1 (Xinhua): Myanmar reopened all basic education schools on Monday, including private schools and Buddhist monastic schools, with a decrease in daily Covid-19 infections in the country.    According to an announcement of Central Committee on Prevention, Control and Treatment for Covid-19, schools in 46 townships of nine regions and states will be excluded from reopening based on the analysis on the test positivity rates per 100,000 people in the past 14 days.    Schools in Yangon region saw less students on Monday, the first day of the reopening.    The authorities closed all schools since early July as part of the anti-pandemic measures.      The Ministry of Health has been administering Covid-19 vaccine doses to middle and high school students aged over 12 since Oct. 12.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220213221252/https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2021/11/01/myanmar-reopens-schools-amid-drop-in-new-covid-19-cases    https://web.archive.org/web/20220213221421/https://en.unesco.org/covid19/educationresponse

column62: 27/1/22  All people over 18 can register for a vaccine.    Has the government of Mauritania approved a COVID-19 vaccine for use?  Yes.  Are vaccines available in Mauritania for U.S. citizens to receive? U.S. citizens (and other non-Mauritanians) over 18 years of age are eligible to receive vaccinations locally by queuing at vaccination centers in Nouakchott.  Due to infrastructure limitations, availability outside Nouakchott is limited.  Which vaccines are available in Mauritania?  The government of Mauritania has approved AstraZeneca, Johnson and Johnson, and SinoPharm.  More information on local availability of COVID-19 vaccines can be found here https://www.sante.gov.mr/?lang=fr .  Visit the FDA’s website to learn more about FDA-approved vaccines in the United States.    The U.S. government does not plan to provide COVID-19 vaccinations to private U.S. citizens overseas. column29: Fully vaccinated international travelers can now enter the island without restrictions. Visitors who present a negative PCR test taken in the 72 hours before their departure can explore the island freely from the moment they arrive.  It is mandatory to arrange COVID-19 insurance health cover (Mauritian citizens, resident permit holders and occupational permit holders are exempted).  COVID-19 testing are required upon arrival day 0 and day 5.  For details, please click here.    Non-vaccinated travelers must show a negative PCR test result 72 hours from the last point of embarkation and COVID-19 insurance health cover.  They must stay in quarantine hotels and are not allowed to leave their room for 14 days. They will have a PCR test on arrival day 0, day 7 and day 14. column43: No change.   COVID-19 Testing:  •	Are PCR and/or antigen tests available for U.S. citizens in Namibia?  Yes  •	If so, are test results reliably available within one calendar day? You may also call +264 83 332 6150.  •	U.S. citizens can also obtain COVID-19 PCR tests in Namibia from the private laboratory PathCare, which has multiple locations throughout the country.  •	Testing costs N$ 750.00 for 48-hour “Standard” processing or N$ 1200.00 for 24-hour “XPRESS” processing. “XPRESS” Processing is only offered at Pathcare’s Eros (Windhoek), Walvisbay, and Ongwediva locations.  •	COVID-19 test results from PathCare are emailed and sent via SMS to the individual who was tested.  •	PathCare tests individuals for the purpose of travel by appointment only.  Please visit https://www.pathcarenamibia.com/ to make an appointment.  •	Feed Masters (Namib Laboratories) is offering a drive through COVID-19 testing facility at the Wanderers Sport Grounds in Pionierspark (Tunchel street) Windhoek.  Hours: Monday to Thursday 07:00 – 19:00, Friday 07:00 -13:00, Saturday, Sunday & Public Holidays 07:00 – 10:00. (24-hours turnaround time).  •	There is no need to make an appointment for this service.  For more information, contact:  Tel.:  061 290 1379; 081 308 4884; Email: namlab@feedmaster.com.na.  •	Fees at the drive-through testing site are:  COVID testing (results 24 hours) – N$ 700.00. column29: As of March 17, 2022, quarantine is no longer required for passengers entering Niger with a negative PCR test.  The PCR test must be less than five (5) days if the traveler is coming from a  UEMOA member country (Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte D’Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal, and Togo).  The PCR test must be less than 72 hours if the traveler is coming from any other country, including the United States.  The Traveler must also be fully vaccinated, the last dose or single dose vaccine must have been taken at least four (4) weeks prior to arrival in Niger.    The measures relating to self-isolation for seven (7) days remain in force for any traveler entering Niger who does not present a negative PCR test dated less than five (5) days if coming from UEMOA member countries, and less than 72 hours for other countries.  The same requirement applies to travelers who are not fully vaccinated, the last dose or single dose vaccine was not taken at least four (4) prior to arrival in Niger. The traveler must undergo a free antigen test for COVID-19 on the 7th day at a site approved by the Nigerien Ministry of Public Health.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220321213324/https://ne.usembassy.gov/u-s-citizen-services/covid-19-information/

Children who are able to go to and from school on their own should do so. Health Minister Luis Francisco Sucre announced in a news conference that Panamanian President Laurentino Cortizo had signed the decree, which mandated public functionaries receive three doses of a coronavirus vaccine or provide proof of a negative COVID-19 test each Monday. column29: /web/20220319205548/https://crisis24.garda.com/alerts/2022/02/panama-authorities-update-some-covid-19-related-travel-measures-as-of-feb-9-update-42  from Feb. 20, travelers arriving in Panama will only be considered fully vaccinated if they have received a booster shot at least 14 days prior to their travel  Travelers who have received all doses of an approved COVID-19 vaccine more than 14 days prior to their arrival in Panama and can show proof of full vaccination may enter the country without the need to take a pre-travel test or to quarantine upon arrival, regardless of their country of origin.    Travelers who are not fully vaccinated must present a negative result from a PCR or antigen test taken within 72 hours prior to their arrival in Panama. Passengers without proof of a negative COVID-19 test result must take a test at the airport and remain there until they have the results. If a traveler tests positive at the airport, they will be placed under quarantine for 14 days at their own expense in a hotel. All travelers must still complete an Online Sworn Affidavit before departure.    Unvaccinated individuals who have been in a designated high-risk country in the 15 days prior to travel to Panama must quarantine for 72 hours upon arrival at an authorized hotel or, if they are Panamanian citizens or residents, at their place of residence. These travelers must take a second test after 72 hours and can leave quarantine if the test is negative. If the result is positive, travelers must isolate for another seven days at their own expense at a government designated location. As of Feb. 9, the countries and territories considered high risk are:    Cayman Islands, Barbados, Anguilla, Bonaire, Greece, Austria, Czech Republic, Estonia, Serbia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovenia, Hungary, Faroe Islands, Ireland, Montenegro, Croatia, Netherlands, Slovakia, Belgium, Bulgaria, Armenia, Ukraine, Jersey, Georgia, Guernsey, the UK, Germany, South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Mozambique, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Malawi.

column29: *update, the extension of emergency health decree on April 1   Supreme Decree No. 030-2022-PCM  https://archive.ph/pif5t    All passengers arriving to Peru aged 12 years or older must show evidence of completed COVID-19 vaccination (final dose received at least 14 days before boarding). Those who are not vaccinated may show proof of a negative result from a PCR test, taken no more than 72 hours before the flight departs. Children under 12 years old must only present without any COVID-19 symptoms. Anyone who shows COVID-19 symptoms on arrival in Peru will be required to isolate. The health authorities are also permitted to perform PCR tests on arriving passengers at the airport and if you receive a positive result, you will be required to isolate. These measures do not apply if you transit through Peru without leaving the airport (remaining airside). You may follow the COVID requirements of your final destination only.    Passengers at the airport will need to follow strict regulations, including the mandatory use of two facemasks and social distancing.    Passengers must complete an Affidavit of Health prior to starting their journey to Peru.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220409080026/https://www.gob.pe/8784  https://web.archive.org/web/20220409080357/https://pe.usembassy.gov/covid-19-information/

column74: Manila: People coming to work in offices in the Philippines will have to get vaccinated against COVID-19 or get tested frequently, the president's office said on Friday, as the country battles one of Asia's worst outbreaks.  A little over a quarter of the Philippines' 110 million population has been fully vaccinated against COVID-19. The government says there are enough stocks available and has been urging people to take the shots.    The new rules for in-office employees will take effect from December 1, Presidential Spokesperson Harry Roque said in a statement. Roque said employees who have not taken the shots even though vaccines are available in their area would be required to undergo tests at their own expense.    Public transportation services will be required to have their employees fully inoculated as a condition to continue their operations, he said.    http://web.archive.org/web/20220204115314/https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/coronavirus-philippines-to-require-covid-vaccination-for-employees-working-in-person-2608157

"On November 29, 2021, the Philippine Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued  an amendment on the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for administration of homologous  and heterologous additional doses to eligible fully vaccinated individuals for the National  COVID-19 Vaccine Deployment Program. column43: Can a test referral only be issued by a GP? Can a doctor from night and holiday telephoto issue such a referral?  An order for a coronavirus test can be issued by a doctor on duty as part of night or holiday health care.    You can also sign up for an online test. All you have to do is fill in the form available at gov.pl/dom . You will be asked to answer a few questions. Based on the data you provide, the system will determine if you qualify for the test.    How it's working?    Go to gov.pl/dom and click the "Form" button.  Answer the survey questions.  If the system qualifies you for the test, a consultant from the Home Medical Care Monitoring Center will contact you.  You will receive an order for the test from the eKolejka system.    https://archive.fo/wXmsk
column45: 14/1/22  No change  Limited contact tracing in place.    I was in close contact with a person who tested positive. Should I report it somewhere?  If you are in close contact with a person infected with the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus (this person has obtained a confirmed, positive PCR test for SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus infection), report this fact to the sanitary inspection. Use the online form: Application for quarantine or isolation by the Sanepid.    If you have questions about quarantine, please call the hotline to contact the sanitary inspection : +48 22 25 00 115. The  hotline is open 24 hours a day.    Important! If you know you have been in close contact with an infected or sick person, stay home - even if you have not yet decided to quarantine, and you are feeling well. Avoid contact with other people. You can infect them if you find out that you are infected. If this is not possible, use all required personal protective equipment.    Attention! If you have been vaccinated for COVID-19, you will not be placed in quarantine. The rule applies from December 28, 2020.    However, from December 15, family  members of people suffering from COVID19 must undergo a coronavirus test, regardless of the certificate they have.    https://archive.fo/wXmsk
column52: 14/1/22  No change to policy      Social distance and face masks  Restrictions on movement  1.5 meters - the minimum distance between pedestrians  Obligation to maintain a distance of at least 1.5 meters between pedestrians.    The following are excluded from this obligation:    parents with children requiring care (up to 13 years of age),  people living together or running a farm,  people with a disability certificate, people with a disability degree, people with a certificate of need for special education, people who are unable to move independently and their guardians.  Covering the mouth and nose only with a mask  Covering the mouth and nose in confined spaces is mandatory throughout the country.  Only cover the nose and mouth with a mask. Scarves, visors and dishes are not allowed because they do not fulfill their primary function, i.e. they do not protect against the virus!    The mouth and nose must be covered, for example:    on the premises of shared properties (e.g. in the staircase),  on the bus, tram and train,  in a shop, shopping mall, bank, market and post office,  in the workplace, if there is more than 1 person in the room (unless the employer decides otherwise),  in the workplace during direct customer / customer service,  in the cinema and theater,  at the doctor's, clinic, hospital, massage and tattoo parlor,  in the church and school, at the university  in offices and other public buildings (in court, cultural institutions, banks, post offices, etc.)  in schools and universities during breaks between lessons and classes, unless otherwise decided by the head of the entity.  Where do you not need to cover your mouth and nose?    In the open air, in the forest, park, greenery, botanical gardens, historic gardens, on roads and squares, in cemeteries, promenades, boulevards, parking places for vehicles, forest parking lots, in family allotments and on the beach, and during private travel by car, motorcycle, quadricycle, moped, at the workplace to eat.     Detailed information on covering the mouth and nose as well as information on exceptions to this rule can be found in the regulation .    Important! Only persons with a medical certificate or a document confirming:    pervasive development disorders,  mental disorders,  moderate, severe or severe intellectual disability,  difficulty uncovering or covering your mouth or nose on your own.  advanced neurological, respiratory or circulatory disorders with respiratory or circulatory failure.    https://archive.fo/yBRsI

column43: 6/2/22    Change in policy. Test are now available for anyone at a pharmacy without prior registration    How to get a coronavirus test at a pharmacy  No signups, no long waiting times and free of charge - now you can get tested at the pharmacy if you are concerned that you have the coronavirus. Check in which pharmacies near you can make it and on what terms!    In the pharmacy, you can do an antigen test:    without prior registration;  free;  unlimited - as many times as you need,  fast - the result after only a dozen or so minutes!  How to do it  Come to the pharmacy where the tests are performed - but be careful! Not every pharmacy participates in the program. Find out where the nearest pharmacy that runs the tests is .  The pharmacist will take a swab.  After a dozen or so minutes, you will receive the result and the pharmacist will enter it in the system.  You can also find information about the result on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .  Test results  If your score is:    negative - you will receive the EU COVID Certificate after the antigen test (valid for 48 hours),  positive - you will start home insulation .  Information on how long your isolation will last and certificates can be found on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .    Attention! Antigen tests are carried out in pharmacies. After a negative antigen test result, you can generate an EU COVID Certificate (UCC), but it will only be valid for 48 hours .    If you fall ill with the coronavirus and confirm the disease with the antigen test, you will not get the convalescent status and the EU COVID Certificate after 10 days!    Recover status confirmed by UCC can only be obtained after confirming the disease with  a PCR test performed at the collection point . Check how to sign up for a test at a download point .    https://web.archive.org/web/20220206124352/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/jak-zrobic-test-na-koronawirusa-w-aptece

Covering the mouth and nose only with a mask  Covering the mouth and nose in confined spaces is mandatory throughout the country.  Only cover the nose and mouth with a mask. Scarves, visors and dishes are not allowed because they do not fulfill their primary function, i.e. they do not protect against the virus!    The mouth and nose must be covered, for example:    on the premises of shared properties (e.g. in the staircase),  on the bus, tram and train,  in a shop, shopping mall, bank, market and post office,  in the workplace, if there is more than 1 person in the room (unless the employer decides otherwise),  in the workplace during direct customer / client service,  in the cinema and theater,  at the doctor's, clinic, hospital, massage and tattoo parlor,  in the church and school, at the university  in offices and other public buildings (in court, cultural institutions, banks, post offices, etc.)  in schools and universities during breaks between lessons and classes, unless otherwise decided by the head of the entity.  Where do you not need to cover your mouth and nose?    In the open air, in the forest, park, greenery, botanical gardens, historic gardens, on roads and squares, in cemeteries, promenades, boulevards, parking places for vehicles, forest parking lots, in family allotments and on the beach, and during private travel by car, motorcycle, quadricycle, moped, at the workplace to eat.     Detailed information on covering the mouth and nose as well as information on exceptions to this rule can be found in the regulation .    Important! Only persons with a medical certificate or a document confirming:    pervasive development disorders,  mental disorders,  moderate, severe or severe intellectual disability,  difficulty uncovering or covering your mouth or nose on your own.  advanced neurological, respiratory or circulatory disorders with respiratory or circulatory failure.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220128094644/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/dystans-spoleczny-i-maseczki

column43: 11/2/22    Change in policy. Test are now available for anyone at a pharmacy without prior registration    How to get a coronavirus test at a pharmacy  No signups, no long waiting times and free of charge - now you can get tested at the pharmacy if you are concerned that you have the coronavirus. Check in which pharmacies near you can make it and on what terms!    In the pharmacy, you can do an antigen test:    without prior registration;  free;  unlimited - as many times as you need,  fast - the result after only a dozen or so minutes!  How to do it  Come to the pharmacy where the tests are performed - but be careful! Not every pharmacy participates in the program. Find out where the nearest pharmacy that runs the tests is .  The pharmacist will take a swab.  After a dozen or so minutes, you will receive the result and the pharmacist will enter it in the system.  You can also find information about the result on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .  Test results  If your score is:    negative - you will receive the EU COVID Certificate after the antigen test (valid for 48 hours),  positive - you will start home insulation .  Information on how long your isolation will last and certificates can be found on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .    Attention! Antigen tests are carried out in pharmacies. After a negative antigen test result, you can generate an EU COVID Certificate (UCC), but it will only be valid for 48 hours .    If you fall ill with the coronavirus and confirm the disease with the antigen test, you will not get the convalescent status and the EU COVID Certificate after 10 days!    Recover status confirmed by UCC can only be obtained after confirming the disease with  a PCR test performed at the collection point . Check how to sign up for a test at a download point .    https://web.archive.org/web/20220206124352/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/jak-zrobic-test-na-koronawirusa-w-aptece
column45: 11/2/22    Limited contact tracing in place.    I was in close contact with a person who tested positive. Should I report it somewhere?  If you are in close contact with a person infected with the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus (this person has obtained a confirmed, positive PCR test for SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus infection), report this fact to the sanitary inspection. Use the online form: Application for quarantine or isolation by the Sanepid.    If you have questions about quarantine, please call the hotline to contact the sanitary inspection : +48 22 25 00 115. The  hotline is open 24 hours a day.    Important! If you know you have been in close contact with an infected or sick person, stay home - even if you have not yet decided to quarantine, and you are feeling well. Avoid contact with other people. You can infect them if you find out that you are infected. If this is not possible, use all required personal protective equipment.    Attention! If you have been vaccinated for COVID-19, you will not be placed in quarantine. The rule applies from December 28, 2020.    However, from December 15, family  members of people suffering from COVID19 must undergo a coronavirus test, regardless of the certificate they have.    https://archive.fo/wXmsk

column55: 11/2/22    We want as many people as possible to receive the preparation against Covid-19 in the shortest possible time. It is in the interest of all of us - the vaccine offers a real chance of recovery.    E-referral    This is the document that entitles you to have the vaccine. In most cases, it is generated automatically for people who can sign up for a vaccination. Only in some cases do patients report to the doctor for this document. This happens when a given person does not have a PESEL number, or in the case of specific patients with the indicated diseases - they are informed about it.    The e-referral is valid for 90 days, but don't hesitate. If you have the opportunity, sign up for the vaccination now!    Registration for vaccination    Anyone who has an e-referral can sign up for a vaccination. There are several ways to do this:    call the helpline 989,  register online via e-Registration,  send an SMS saying SzczepimySie to the number 880 333 333,  sign up directly at the vaccination point (preferably by phone),  use the drive-thru point .     https://web.archive.org/web/20220127030346/https://www.gov.pl/web/szczepimysie/jak-sie--zaszczepic

column15: Attention! The number of persons vaccinated against COVID-19 is not counted if they show:    EU digital COVID certificate;  or a certificate of vaccination, test result and recovery. Concerts and circus performances  Events may take place under the following conditions:    making available to viewers or listeners no more than 30 percent. number of seats,    keep a distance of 1.5 m between viewers or listeners in the absence of designated seats in the audience and ensure that no more than 1 person per 15 square meters is present in the room at the same time,    ensure that viewers or listeners comply with the order to cover their mouth and nose.    Concerts and circus performances may be organized outdoors under the following conditions:    making available to viewers or listeners no more than 30 percent. number of seats,    keep a distance of 1.5 m between viewers or listeners in the absence of designated seats in the audience,    ensure that viewers or listeners comply with the order to cover their mouth and nose.    Outdoor amusement parks  Amusement parks may operate at up to 30%. occupancy.    Libraries  Possibility to make collections available, provided that no more than 1 person per 15 m² is present in the library, with the exception of librarians. Before entering the library, information about the limit of people should be posted.    Conducting activities by public and scientific libraries consisting in the organization of meetings and events is allowed indoors, provided that:    while maintaining a distance of 1.5 m between participants;    that participants comply with the obligation to cover their mouth and nose.    Night clubs, discos and other places available for dancing  Nightclubs, discos and other places to dance have closed.    Fairs, exhibitions, congresses, conferences  Trade fairs, congresses and conferences can be organized within the limit of 1 person per 15 m2.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220128093751/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/kultura-i-rozrywka

column29: Rules for travelers coming to Poland from European Union Member States, from the Schengen area and others  If you are traveling with:    European Union Member States,  Switzerland  Iceland,  Norway  Liechtenstein,  Principality of Andorra,  Principalities of Monaco,  The Republic of San Marino,  Vatican City State  you are subject to a 7-day quarantine.     You are not quarantined if:    you are vaccinated with the full vaccination course:  a vaccine that is authorized in the European Union or is included in the list of vaccine equivalents authorized for marketing in the territory of the Republic of Poland, kept by the National Institute of Public Health PZH - National Research Institute,  14 days have elapsed since the administration of the last dose of vaccination (counted from the day following the administration of the last dose),  vaccination is certified by the EU digital COVID certificate or other document in Polish or English confirming the vaccination.  You have been infected with the SARS-CoV-2 virus (you are the so-called healer):  not later than 6 months before the day of crossing the PR border,  you have a document that confirms the presence of the disease, issued in Polish or English, including the EU COVID Certificate,  You will present a negative COVID-19 test result:  certified by the EU digital COVID certificate or other document in Polish or English,  the test must be performed no earlier than 48 hours before crossing the border,  You are 12 or under and traveling with adults who are vaccinated against COVID-19 or tested negative for COVID-19.  You are subject to other exemptions listed in § 3 of the Regulation of the Council of Ministers of May 6, 2021 on the establishment of certain restrictions, orders and bans in connection with the occurrence of an epidemic.  If you have been quarantined, you can perform a test up to 48 hours after crossing the border, the negative result of which will release you from quarantine.    Also check who is exempt from the obligation to quarantine after crossing the state border.    What test can I do?    Test type: RT-PCR and antigen test.  Tests are not publicly funded.  Are you a foreigner?    Check the border crossing rules for foreigners.    Traveler Location Card  A person who crosses the state border of the Republic of Poland by plane fills in the Traveler Location Card in an electronic form before check-in , and if this is not possible - a paper-based travel location card provided by the cabin crew.    The data administrator is the state poviat sanitary inspector competent for the place of residence or stay of the traveler.    EU COVID Certificate  The EU COVID Certificate is issued by the Ministry of Health. A vaccination certificate is issued:    in electronic form,  in paper form;  by providers of immunization against COVID-19,  by a primary care physician or primary care nurse.  Detailed information on the EU COVID Certificate .    Important! This communication is provided for information purposes only and cannot be used as a basis for adjudicating on a case-by-case basis. The verification on the basis of the document presented for inspection and the final decision on quarantine or grounds for exemption from such a requirement will be taken by a Border Guard officer who performs border control.    In disputed / doubtful / random matters regarding sanitary restrictions / quarantine / vaccinations - including the rules for exemptions, shortening its duration - the only competent authority is the State (Border) Sanitary Inspector at the local level, or a higher level authority, i.e. the Minister responsible for Health (Chief Sanitary Inspector).    https://web.archive.org/web/20220221121222/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/przyjazd-do-polski-ze-strefy-schengen

column43: 25/2/22  Change in policy. Test are now available for anyone at a pharmacy without prior registration    How to get a coronavirus test at a pharmacy  No signups, no long waiting times and free of charge - now you can get tested at the pharmacy if you are concerned that you have the coronavirus. Check in which pharmacies near you can make it and on what terms!    In the pharmacy, you can do an antigen test:    without prior registration;  free;  unlimited - as many times as you need,  fast - the result after only a dozen or so minutes!  How to do it  Come to the pharmacy where the tests are performed - but be careful! Not every pharmacy participates in the program. Find out where the nearest pharmacy that runs the tests is .  The pharmacist will take a swab.  After a dozen or so minutes, you will receive the result and the pharmacist will enter it in the system.  You can also find information about the result on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .  Test results  If your score is:    negative - you will receive the EU COVID Certificate after the antigen test (valid for 48 hours),  positive - you will start home insulation .  Information on how long your isolation will last and certificates can be found on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .    Attention! Antigen tests are carried out in pharmacies. After a negative antigen test result, you can generate an EU COVID Certificate (UCC), but it will only be valid for 48 hours .    If you fall ill with the coronavirus and confirm the disease with the antigen test, you will not get the convalescent status and the EU COVID Certificate after 10 days!    Recover status confirmed by UCC can only be obtained after confirming the disease with  a PCR test performed at the collection point . Check how to sign up for a test at a download point .      https://web.archive.org/web/20220204154012/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/zapisz-sie-na-test-na-koronawirusa

column29: 4/3/22  Rules for travelers coming to Poland from outside the European Union and from outside the Schengen area  Mandatory COVID-19 tests  People traveling from outside the European Union, from outside the Schengen area, must show a negative COVID-19 test result. You must complete the test regardless of the way in which you travel (collective, individual or on foot). Failure to test will require quarantine.    The obligation to perform the test also applies to vaccinated people or convalescents!    The test result must not be more than 24 hours prior to arrival.  The test can be performed at some airports in Poland - before border clearance or 3 hours after arrival (counting from border clearance).  quarantine   Attention! Persons crossing the Polish-Ukrainian border due to an armed conflict in Ukraine are not currently subject to the obligation to quarantine entry.    You are not quarantined if your antigen or PCR test is negative  and you meet one of the following conditions :    you are vaccinated with the full vaccination course:  a vaccine that is authorized in the European Union or is included in the list of vaccine equivalents authorized for marketing in the territory of the Republic of Poland, kept by the National Institute of Public Health PZH - National Research Institute,  14 days have elapsed since the administration of the last dose of vaccination (counted from the day following the administration of the last dose),  vaccination is certified by the EU COVID Certificate or another document in Polish or English confirming the vaccination.  You have been infected with the SARS-CoV-2 virus (you are the so-called healer):  not later than 6 months before the day of crossing the PR border,  you have a document that confirms the presence of the disease, issued in Polish or English, including the EU COVID Certificate .  You are subject to other exemptions listed in § 3 of the Regulation of the Council of Ministers of May 6, 2021 on the establishment of certain restrictions, orders and bans in connection with the occurrence of an epidemic.  Who is exempt from showing COVID-19 test results when arriving from outside the Schengen area?       Important! If you do not submit a negative test result, you must go into quarantine for  7 days .      What test can I do?    before crossing the border: RT-PCR or antigenic.  Tests are not publicly funded.    Important!     Persons who, after arriving from outside the Schengen area, the EU, stay in the territory of the Republic of Poland for no longer than 24 hours and have a flight ticket confirming departure from the territory of the Republic of Poland within 24 hours, may be exempt from the obligation to undergo quarantine, provided that:    show a negative result of the SARS-CoV-2 test (antigenic, PCR) performed within 24 hours before arrival to the Republic of Poland,  perform such a test before the border check (applies only to airports where it is possible),  perform the test at the airport after the border check within 3 hours.  Traveler Location Card  Each person who crosses the state border of the Republic of Poland by plane fills in the Traveler Location Card in an electronic form before check-in . If this is not possible, fill it in on a paper form provided by the cabin crew.    The data administrator is the state poviat sanitary inspector (sanepid) competent for the place of residence or stay of the traveler.    EU COVID Certificate  The EU COVID Certificate is issued by the Ministry of Health. A vaccination certificate is issued:    in electronic form,  in paper form;  by providers of immunization against COVID-19,  by a primary care physician or primary care nurse.  Detailed information on the  EU COVID Certificate .    Also check the  Border Guard website for information on quarantine after crossing the border.    Important! This communication is provided for information purposes only and cannot be used as a basis for adjudicating on a case-by-case basis. The verification on the basis of the document presented for inspection and the final decision on quarantine or grounds for exemption from such a requirement will be taken by a Border Guard officer who performs border control.    In disputed / doubtful / random matters regarding sanitary restrictions / quarantine / vaccinations - including the rules for exemptions, shortening its duration - the only competent authority is the State (Border) Sanitary Inspector at the local level, or a higher level authority, i.e. the Minister responsible for Health (Chief Sanitary Inspector).    https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/przyjazd-do-polski-spoza-strefy-schengen

column43: 11/3/22  Change in policy. Test are now available for anyone at a pharmacy without prior registration    How to get a coronavirus test at a pharmacy  No signups, no long waiting times and free of charge - now you can get tested at the pharmacy if you are concerned that you have the coronavirus. Check in which pharmacies near you can make it and on what terms!    In the pharmacy, you can do an antigen test:    without prior registration;  free;  unlimited - as many times as you need,  fast - the result after only a dozen or so minutes!  How to do it  Come to the pharmacy where the tests are performed - but be careful! Not every pharmacy participates in the program. Find out where the nearest pharmacy that runs the tests is .  The pharmacist will take a swab.  After a dozen or so minutes, you will receive the result and the pharmacist will enter it in the system.  You can also find information about the result on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .  Test results  If your score is:    negative - you will receive the EU COVID Certificate after the antigen test (valid for 48 hours),  positive - you will start home insulation .  Information on how long your isolation will last and certificates can be found on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .    Attention! Antigen tests are carried out in pharmacies. After a negative antigen test result, you can generate an EU COVID Certificate (UCC), but it will only be valid for 48 hours .    If you fall ill with the coronavirus and confirm the disease with the antigen test, you will not get the convalescent status and the EU COVID Certificate after 10 days!    Recover status confirmed by UCC can only be obtained after confirming the disease with  a PCR test performed at the collection point . Check how to sign up for a test at a download point .      https://web.archive.org/web/20220204154012/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/zapisz-sie-na-test-na-koronawirusa
column45: 11/3/22  Limited contact tracing in place.    I was in close contact with a person who tested positive. Should I report it somewhere?  If you are in close contact with a person infected with the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus (this person has obtained a confirmed, positive PCR test for SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus infection), report this fact to the sanitary inspection. Use the online form: Application for quarantine or isolation by the Sanepid.    If you have questions about quarantine, please call the hotline to contact the sanitary inspection : +48 22 25 00 115. The  hotline is open 24 hours a day.    Important! If you know you have been in close contact with an infected or sick person, stay home - even if you have not yet decided to quarantine, and you are feeling well. Avoid contact with other people. You can infect them if you find out that you are infected. If this is not possible, use all required personal protective equipment.    Attention! If you have been vaccinated for COVID-19, you will not be placed in quarantine. The rule applies from December 28, 2020.    However, from December 15, family  members of people suffering from COVID19 must undergo a coronavirus test, regardless of the certificate they have.    https://archive.fo/wXmsk
column52: 11/3/22  Masks must be worn in enclosed spaces throughout Poland    Covering the mouth and nose only with a mask  Covering the mouth and nose in confined spaces is mandatory throughout the country.  Only cover the nose and mouth with a mask. Scarves, visors and dishes are not allowed because they do not fulfill their primary function, i.e. they do not protect against the virus!    The mouth and nose must be covered, for example:    on the premises of shared properties (e.g. in the staircase),  on the bus, tram and train,  in a shop, shopping mall, bank, market and post office,  in the workplace, if there is more than 1 person in the room (unless the employer decides otherwise),  in the workplace during direct customer / client service,  in the cinema and theater,  at the doctor's, clinic, hospital, massage and tattoo parlor,  in the church and school, at the university  in offices and other public buildings (in court, cultural institutions, banks, post offices, etc.)  in schools and universities during breaks between lessons and classes, unless otherwise decided by the head of the entity.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220304082256/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/dystans-spoleczny-i-maseczki
column55: 11/3/22  We want as many people as possible to receive the preparation against Covid-19 in the shortest possible time. It is in the interest of all of us - the vaccine offers a real chance of recovery.    E-referral    This is the document that entitles you to have the vaccine. In most cases, it is generated automatically for people who can sign up for a vaccination. Only in some cases do patients report to the doctor for this document. This happens when a given person does not have a PESEL number, or in the case of specific patients with the indicated diseases - they are informed about it.    The e-referral is valid for 90 days, but don't hesitate. If you have the opportunity, sign up for the vaccination now!    Registration for vaccination    Anyone who has an e-referral can sign up for a vaccination. There are several ways to do this:    call the helpline 989,  register online via e-Registration,  send an SMS saying SzczepimySie to the number 880 333 333,  sign up directly at the vaccination point (preferably by phone),  use the drive-thru point .     https://web.archive.org/web/20220127030346/https://www.gov.pl/web/szczepimysie/jak-sie--zaszczepic

column74: Are vaccinations voluntary?  Vaccination is voluntary, except for healthcare professionals, pharmacists, medical students and healthcare professionals who must be fully vaccinated by March 1, 2022. We encourage other people to vaccinate against COVID-19. The more people get vaccinated, the more effective protection against the coronavirus will be.     https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.gov.pl/web/szczepimysie/pytania-i-odpowiedzi

column43: No change    No change    Change in policy. Test are now available for anyone at a pharmacy without prior registration    How to get a coronavirus test at a pharmacy  No signups, no long waiting times and free of charge - now you can get tested at the pharmacy if you are concerned that you have the coronavirus. Check in which pharmacies near you can make it and on what terms!    In the pharmacy, you can do an antigen test:    without prior registration;  free;  unlimited - as many times as you need,  fast - the result after only a dozen or so minutes!  How to do it  Come to the pharmacy where the tests are performed - but be careful! Not every pharmacy participates in the program. Find out where the nearest pharmacy that runs the tests is .  The pharmacist will take a swab.  After a dozen or so minutes, you will receive the result and the pharmacist will enter it in the system.  You can also find information about the result on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .  Test results  If your score is:    negative - you will receive the EU COVID Certificate after the antigen test (valid for 48 hours),  positive - you will start home insulation .  Information on how long your isolation will last and certificates can be found on the Internet Patient Account and in the mojeIKP application .    Attention! Antigen tests are carried out in pharmacies. After a negative antigen test result, you can generate an EU COVID Certificate (UCC), but it will only be valid for 48 hours .    If you fall ill with the coronavirus and confirm the disease with the antigen test, you will not get the convalescent status and the EU COVID Certificate after 10 days!    Recover status confirmed by UCC can only be obtained after confirming the disease with  a PCR test performed at the collection point . Check how to sign up for a test at a download point .      https://web.archive.org/web/20220204154012/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/zapisz-sie-na-test-na-koronawirusa
column45: No change  Limited contact tracing in place.    I was in close contact with a person who tested positive. Should I report it somewhere?  If you are in close contact with a person infected with the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus (this person has obtained a confirmed, positive PCR test for SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus infection), report this fact to the sanitary inspection. Use the online form: Application for quarantine or isolation by the Sanepid.    If you have questions about quarantine, please call the hotline to contact the sanitary inspection : +48 22 25 00 115. The  hotline is open 24 hours a day.    Important! If you know you have been in close contact with an infected or sick person, stay home - even if you have not yet decided to quarantine, and you are feeling well. Avoid contact with other people. You can infect them if you find out that you are infected. If this is not possible, use all required personal protective equipment.    Attention! If you have been vaccinated for COVID-19, you will not be placed in quarantine. The rule applies from December 28, 2020.    However, from December 15, family  members of people suffering from COVID19 must undergo a coronavirus test, regardless of the certificate they have.    https://archive.fo/wXmsk
column52: Covering the mouth and nose only with a mask  Covering the mouth and nose in confined spaces is mandatory throughout the country.  Only cover the nose and mouth with a mask. Scarves, visors and dishes are not allowed because they do not fulfill their primary function, i.e. they do not protect against the virus!    The mouth and nose must be covered, for example:    on the premises of shared properties (e.g. in the staircase),  on the bus, tram and train,  in a shop, shopping mall, bank, market and post office,  in the workplace, if there is more than 1 person in the room (unless the employer decides otherwise),  in the workplace during direct customer / customer service,  in the cinema and theater,  at the doctor's, clinic, hospital, massage and tattoo parlor,  in the church and school, at the university  in offices and other public buildings (in court, cultural institutions, banks, post offices, etc.)  in schools and universities during breaks between lessons and classes, unless otherwise decided by the head of the entity.  Where do you not need to cover your mouth and nose?    In the open air, in the forest, park, greenery, botanical gardens, historic gardens, on roads and squares, in cemeteries, promenades, boulevards, parking places for vehicles, forest parking lots, in family allotments and on the beach, and during private travel by car, motorcycle, quadricycle, moped, at the workplace to eat.     Detailed information on covering the mouth and nose as well as information on exceptions to this rule can be found in the regulation .    https://web.archive.org/web/20220317052425/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/aktualne-zasady-i-ograniczenia
column55: 1/4/22  No change  How to get vaccinated?  The pass for vaccination is e-referral. Currently, children from 5 years of age can get vaccinated. There are a few basic rules to follow right before vaccination. Read on for details.    We want as many people as possible to receive the preparation against Covid-19 in the shortest possible time. It is in the interest of all of us - the vaccine offers a real chance of recovery.    E-referral    This is the document that entitles you to have the vaccine. In most cases, it is generated automatically for people who can sign up for a vaccination. Only in some cases do patients report to the doctor for this document. This happens when a given person does not have a PESEL number, or in the case of specific patients with the indicated diseases - they are informed about it.    The e-referral is valid for 90 days, but don't hesitate. If you have the opportunity, sign up for the vaccination now!    Registration for vaccination    Anyone who has an e-referral can sign up for a vaccination. There are several ways to do this:    call the helpline 989,  register online via e-Registration,  send an SMS saying SzczepimySie to the number 880 333 333,  mojeIKP - mobile application,  sign up directly at the vaccination point (preferably by phone),  use the drive-thru point .     Register for vaccination - find out the details    How to prepare for vaccinations *?    Get enough sleep before vaccination - sleep has a positive effect on the immune system.  Limit alcohol - a few days before vaccination, but also after taking the preparation, reduce the amount, and preferably do not consume alcohol at all.  Be physically active before vaccination - exercise improves your body's performance.  You do not need to fast before having the vaccine - eat all meals as normal on the day of vaccination.  Do not stop taking the medications you regularly take on your own - consult your doctor.  Carefully complete the pre-vaccination questionnaire - you will be asked to complete a medical questionnaire before taking the preparation. Don't withhold any information!  Wait after vaccination at the vaccination site of min . 15 minutes - it's for your safety.  Do not be afraid of NOP - it is short for undesirable vaccine reactions. They are mostly mild and rare. It may happen that after receiving the vaccine you will have, for example, redness at the injection site or a mild fever. These symptoms should disappear within 1-3 days. If you are more uncomfortable, you can take an anti-pyretic drug after vaccination.    https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.gov.pl/web/szczepimysie/jak-sie--zaszczepic

column43: 1/4/22  From April 1, 2022, the rules for ordering and performing coronavirus tests will change.  Your doctor will decide to refer you for a coronavirus test based on an assessment of your health, including symptoms that may indicate COVID-19. .  If a GP decides to test a patient with disturbing symptoms, it will be a rapid antigen test. The test result is known after a few or several minutes. The test will be free for the patient.  A PCR test may be ordered by your doctor prior to admission to hospital if deemed necessary. The PCR test will be used in the event of definitive confirmation or exclusion of whether the symptoms of respiratory tract infections with which the patient entered the hospital are caused by the coronavirus.  In the case of a positive SARS-CoV-2 test result, the doctor recommends self-isolation (sick leave) until symptoms disappear. Just like any infectious disease, such as the flu.  The length of the sick leave depends on the doctor (minimum 7 days recommended), depending on the patient's condition, risk factors for the severe course of the COVID-19 disease (e.g. lack of vaccination against COVID-19, advanced age, chronic diseases, e.g. diabetes) and high risk the occurrence of complications.    https://web.archive.org/web/2/https://www.gov.pl/web/koronawirus/zapisz-sie-na-test-na-koronawirusa
